brief.meaningEn: Throughout all the areas or members of the relevant group.
brief.meaningZh: 在所指範圍的各部分或所有成員之中。
brief.grammar: A change applies across the board; identify the relevant group and distinguish broad coverage from an identical amount.
brief.register: Established idiom for comprehensive scope, not a literal board.
brief.boundaryZh: 範圍由情境界定；各項都改變，不表示幅度完全相同或連未提及範圍也包括。
brief.misconceptionZh: 所有類別受影響與所有類別增加同一數額不同。
brief.outcomeZh: 能清楚說明全面適用的範圍及仍需分別核對的細節。

listening.promptZh: 費用變動的範圍是甚麼？

options.en: All three class levels cost more, with different increases.
options.zh: 三個程度的班都較貴，但加幅不同。

options.en: Only the advanced classes cost more this term.
options.zh: 本學期只有高級班較貴。

options.en: Each class level received exactly the same increase.
options.zh: 每個程度的班加費完全相同。

options.en: The beginner class kept its previous fee.
options.zh: 初級班維持原有費用。

listening.explanationZh: 三個程度都加費說明涵蓋範圍；different保留幅度差異。
listening.en: The workshop raised fees across the board: the beginner, intermediate and advanced classes all cost more this term, though the increases were different.
listening.zh: 工作坊全面加費：初、中、高級班本學期都較貴，但加幅不同。

reply.promptEn: Which workshop classes became more expensive?
reply.promptZh: 工作坊哪些班變得較貴？

options.en: The beginner, intermediate and advanced classes all did.
options.zh: 初、中、高級班都加費了。

options.en: Fees rose across the board, although not by the same amount.
options.zh: 所有班別都加費，但幅度不一。

options.en: Every class level listed in the notice now costs more.
options.zh: 通告所列的每個程度現在都較貴。

options.en: The change affected all three levels rather than just the advanced group.
options.zh: 改動影響三個程度，不只有高級組。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代已列三個程度全部受影響，不把加幅當相同。

scene.promptZh: 社區刊物三個欄目都改用較大字體，但標題仍各有大小。編輯想描述內文字體政策的涵蓋範圍。哪句準確？

options.en: The larger body text was introduced across the board in the three sections.
options.zh: 三個欄目全面採用較大內文字體。

options.en: The change was limited to the first section.
options.zh: 改動只限第一欄目。

options.en: The policy made every heading the same size.
options.zh: 政策令每個標題大小相同。

scene.explanationZh: 全面適用於三欄內文，不擴張到標題，也不縮成只改一欄。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 across the board 推出？

options.en: The stated change covers the whole relevant group.
options.zh: 所述改變涵蓋整個相關群體。

options.en: The size of the change is identical in each case.
options.zh: 每個個案的改變幅度完全相同。

options.en: The context is needed to identify the group concerned.
options.zh: 需情境指出所涉及的群體。

contrast.explanationZh: 這個用語說範圍；相同幅度要另有資料。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把工作坊通告寫成所有班都加同一費用，但通告列出不同加幅。你怎回應？

options.en: The rise applies across the board, but we should report the different amounts for each level.
options.zh: 所有班別都加費，但我們應列出各程度不同的加幅。

options.en: We can use the advanced-class increase as the amount for the beginner class too.
options.zh: 我們也可把高級班加幅當作初級班加幅。

options.en: The different amounts mean the change affected only one level.
options.zh: 加幅不同表示改動只影響一個程度。

dialogue.explanationZh: 區分全面涵蓋與各項數字，不以一項數額代替其他程度。

speaking.en: The changes apply across the board, but their effects still need to be checked in each section.
speaking.zh: 改動全面適用，但仍需核對各部分的影響。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說清範圍及個別細節。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：活動小組想規定所有義工都先看安全簡報，包括熟手；實際崗位示範則按工作另排。你要寫一句通告，交代共同要求及不同安排。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The safety briefing applies across the board, including experienced volunteers. Demonstrations will then be arranged for the different roles.
examples.zh: 安全簡報適用於所有義工，包括熟手；之後會按不同崗位安排示範。

examples.en: We will require the safety briefing across the board, while keeping the practical demonstrations specific to each role.
examples.zh: 我們會要求所有義工先看安全簡報，而實際示範仍按各崗位需要安排。

writing.selfCheckZh: 所有義工有共同簡報要求，但崗位示範仍不同；不要把全面適用說成所有培訓內容一樣。

takeaways.en: The library extended loan periods across the board, including the smaller branches.
takeaways.zh: 圖書館全面延長借閱期，包括較小的分館。

takeaways.en: The new review date applies across the board to the projects listed in the notice.
takeaways.zh: 通告所列的項目全面適用於新的檢討日期。

lessons.titleZh: 必要時轉而依靠備用選擇

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: He may fall back on takeaway after a late shift.

brief.meaningEn: Use an available alternative when the preferred option is unavailable or unsuccessful.
brief.meaningZh: 首選不可用或不奏效時，轉用可依靠的替代選擇。
brief.grammar: fall back on + resource/person/plan; fell/fallen; specify the difficulty and the available alternative.
brief.register: Common phrasal verb for a reserve option; not necessarily a bad or shameful choice.
brief.boundaryZh: 需有備用依靠的情境，不只是按喜好選東西；備用也要實際可用。
brief.misconceptionZh: 備用選擇可以有幫助，不等於首選已修好或問題完全解決。
brief.outcomeZh: 能交代首選遇到甚麼限制，以及哪項替代資源有何作用。

options.en: They allowed the route explanation to continue without the projector.
options.zh: 它們讓路線解釋可在沒有投影機下繼續。

options.en: They were the first-choice format before any equipment problem.
options.zh: 器材出問題前，它們本來就是首選形式。

options.en: The film had already finished before the projector stopped working.
options.zh: 投影機停用前，短片已放映完畢。

options.en: The diagrams were used to repair the projector rather than explain the route.
options.zh: 圖表是用來修投影機，而非解釋路線。

listening.explanationZh: 圖表讓路線解釋繼續，卻沒有修好投影機；短片仍待設備修好，不是已放映。
listening.en: When the projector stopped working, we fell back on the printed diagrams to explain the route; the short film had to wait until the equipment was repaired.
listening.zh: 投影機停用時，我們轉用印好的圖表解釋路線；短片則需等器材修好。

reply.promptEn: How did you explain the route when the projector failed?
reply.promptZh: 投影機故障後，你們怎樣解釋路線？

options.en: We used the diagrams we already had on paper.
options.zh: 我們用了已有的紙本圖表。

options.en: We fell back on the printed diagrams as an alternative.
options.zh: 我們轉而依靠紙本圖表作替代。

options.en: The paper copies let us continue explaining the route.
options.zh: 紙本讓我們繼續解釋路線。

options.en: We had another way to present the route while the film was unavailable.
options.zh: 短片不能播放時，我們有另一種介紹路線的方法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應故障時的替代做法，不聲稱短片已放映。

scene.promptZh: 你原想請懂當地歷史的鄰居講解，對方臨時有事；你改用他預先授權的錄音，另記觀眾問題待他回覆。哪句貼切？

options.en: We can fall back on his recording and save the questions for later.
options.zh: 我們可轉用他的錄音，把問題留待之後回覆。

options.en: The audience has already received his answers to the new questions.
options.zh: 觀眾已收到他對新問題的回覆。

options.en: The recording means he has agreed to attend in person after all.
options.zh: 錄音表示他終於同意親自出席。

scene.explanationZh: 可用授權錄音替代現場講解，但新問題仍待回覆。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 fall back on 的備用意思？

options.en: Using a reserve resource when the preferred method fails.
options.zh: 首選方法失效時，使用備用資源。

options.en: Choosing the preferred method while it remains available, with no need for an alternative.
options.zh: 首選仍可用且不需替代時，選用首選方法。

options.en: Turning to an available helper when the planned support is absent.
options.zh: 原定支援缺席時，轉而依靠可幫忙的人。

contrast.explanationZh: 首選順利用上，不是遇到限制後轉向備用。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說既然圖表可備用，就可把通告寫成短片照常播放；但投影機仍待修。哪句回應最好？

options.en: We can fall back on the diagrams for the route, but we should say that the film is postponed.
options.zh: 我們可轉用圖表講路線，但應說明短片延期。

options.en: The notice can keep the original film time because we have paper diagrams.
options.zh: 我們有紙本圖表，所以通告可保留原來的短片放映時間。

options.en: We should cancel the route explanation even though the diagrams are ready.
options.zh: 即使圖表已準備好，我們仍應取消路線解釋。

dialogue.explanationZh: 替代資源維持部分活動，同時準確交代短片限制。

speaking.en: We can fall back on the paper copies if the display fails, although they cannot show the animation.
speaking.zh: 螢幕故障時可轉用紙本，但紙本不能展示動畫。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說明備用方法與限制。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你整理家族故事，本想核對舊信原件，卻暫時借不到；你可先用有日期的掃描本寫草稿，把看不清的字標為待核。用一至兩句英文說明臨時做法，不把草稿當已核實。

examples.en: I can fall back on the dated scans to draft the family story while the original letters are unavailable. I will mark the unclear words for checking later.
examples.zh: 原信暫不可借時，我可先依靠有日期的掃描本寫家族故事草稿，並把看不清的字標出，留待之後核對。

examples.en: We will fall back on the scans for a first draft, but the uncertain readings must remain marked until we can examine the letters.
examples.zh: 我們會先用掃描本寫初稿，但讀法不確定的地方須保留標記，直至能檢視原信。

writing.selfCheckZh: 備用掃描本讓草稿可開始，但仍標明不清字句及待核狀態。

takeaways.en: The singers fell back on an acoustic arrangement when the sound system failed.
takeaways.zh: 音響故障時，歌手轉用原音編曲。

takeaways.en: I keep a saved map to fall back on when the connection is unavailable.
takeaways.zh: 我保留離線地圖，供沒有連線時使用。

lessons.titleZh: 暫時快速解決問題的方法

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Healthy habits need more than quick fixes.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Healthy habits need more than quick fixes.

sources.sentence: Healthy habits need more than quick fixes.

brief.meaningEn: A fast solution, often temporary or insufficient for an underlying problem.
brief.meaningZh: 快速的解決辦法，常屬暫時性，未必處理根本問題。
brief.grammar: a quick fix for + problem; quick fixes; identify what is temporarily improved and what remains.
brief.register: Established informal noun phrase. Quick does not automatically mean ineffective; assess the actual result.
brief.boundaryZh: 快速方法可有暫時用途，不應一概說無用；但不能把表面改善當原因已解決。
brief.misconceptionZh: 分清即時紓緩、長期處理及尚未查明的原因。
brief.outcomeZh: 能評估快速做法的作用與限制，提出相關後續工作。

listening.promptZh: 改名解決了甚麼，仍欠甚麼？

options.en: It improved immediate access, while responsibility for maintaining versions remained unsettled.
options.zh: 它即時改善找檔案，但維護版本的責任仍未議定。

options.en: It established a named person responsible for future versions.
options.zh: 它已確立負責日後版本的指定人員。

options.en: It made finding files harder that afternoon.
options.zh: 它令當天下午更難找檔案。

options.en: It was intended only to change the public title of the archive.
options.zh: 它只是想改檔案庫對外的名稱。

listening.explanationZh: 當天下午找檔案較容易，但重複版本持續，維護責任未定。
listening.en: Renaming the confusing folders was a quick fix that helped us find files that afternoon, but duplicate versions kept appearing because nobody had agreed who would maintain the archive.
listening.zh: 把混亂的資料夾改名，是當天下午有助找檔案的快速辦法；但大家未議定誰維護檔案庫，重複版本仍出現。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want to discuss responsibility after renaming the folders?
reply.promptZh: 資料夾改名後，你為甚麼仍想討論負責安排？

options.en: The new names helped us search, but duplicate versions are still being added.
options.zh: 新名稱有助搜尋，但重複版本仍在增加。

options.en: The quick fix improved access without settling who maintains the archive.
options.zh: 快速辦法改善找檔案，卻未定誰維護檔案庫。

options.en: We still need someone to manage versions rather than only clearer labels.
options.zh: 除了清楚標示，我們仍需有人管理版本。

options.en: The immediate improvement did not resolve the continuing source of confusion.
options.zh: 即時改善並未解決持續混亂的來源。

reply.explanationZh: 四句承認眼前改善，也指出維護安排尚欠，不把暫時方法說成全無用途。

scene.promptZh: 社團通知太多，成員漏看工作；把本周急事置頂可先幫忙，但長期仍需議定發布渠道。哪句準確？

options.en: Pinning the urgent note is a useful quick fix, while the communication process still needs review.
options.zh: 把急事置頂是有用的快速辦法，但溝通流程仍需檢討。

options.en: Pinning one note has already established the group’s long-term posting rules.
options.zh: 把一則消息置頂，已確立小組長期發布規則。

options.en: The urgent note has been removed so members cannot see it.
options.zh: 急事通知已刪除，成員不能看見。

scene.explanationZh: 置頂能暫時提醒，長期渠道規則仍未議定。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 quick fix 推出？

options.en: A solution can be put into use quickly.
options.zh: 辦法可迅速實行。

options.en: The underlying cause has definitely been removed.
options.zh: 根本原因已確實消除。

options.en: The context may show that further work is needed.
options.zh: 情境可能顯示仍需後續工作。

contrast.explanationZh: 快速描述實行速度，不能單憑它確立根本原因已消失。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說資料夾改名後不用再談維護人，但重複版本仍增加。哪句回應最好？

options.en: The quick fix helped today; now we need to agree who will check and maintain the versions.
options.zh: 快速辦法今天有幫助；現在需議定誰核對及維護版本。

options.en: We can close the maintenance discussion because the folder names are clearer.
options.zh: 資料夾名稱清楚了，所以可結束維護討論。

options.en: We should restore the confusing names before deciding who maintains the files.
options.zh: 決定誰維護檔案前，我們應恢復混亂的名稱。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留有效的即時改善，另處理持續產生重複版本的責任問題。

speaking.en: The quick fix made the page easier to use, but we still need to investigate why the errors keep returning.
speaking.zh: 快速辦法令網頁較易用，但我們仍需查錯誤為何反覆出現。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再區分即時改善與持續原因。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：舞台模型的一角不穩，臨時支撐令展示可繼續，但你尚未查接合位為何鬆。你要在交接筆記中交代當下狀態及展示後檢查，不作安全保證。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The temporary support was a quick fix that let the model stay on display. We still need to examine the loose joint afterwards.
examples.zh: 臨時支撐是讓模型可繼續展示的快速辦法；之後仍需檢查鬆動接合位。

examples.en: Our quick fix steadied the model for the demonstration, but it did not explain why the joint had loosened. Please keep the inspection on the handover list.
examples.zh: 快速辦法在示範時穩住模型，但未解釋接合位為何變鬆；請把檢查保留在交接清單上。

writing.selfCheckZh: 描述模型暫時穩住及後續檢查，不把臨時支撐當已查明原因或安全認證。

takeaways.en: A clearer sign was a quick fix while we redesigned the booking process.
takeaways.zh: 重新設計預約流程期間，較清楚的標示是快速應對辦法。

takeaways.en: The editor accepted the quick fix for this issue but scheduled a fuller review before the next one.
takeaways.zh: 編輯接受本期的快速辦法，但安排下期前作較全面檢討。

lessons.titleZh: 要求或判準已改變

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The goalposts have moved in modern education.

brief.meaningEn: The criteria or expectations have changed from those previously used.
brief.meaningZh: 原有的判準或期望已經改變。
brief.grammar: the goalposts have/had moved; explain previous and new expectations. Agentive move the goalposts often implies unfair changing of rules; the intransitive frame need not establish blame.
brief.register: Established sporting metaphor. Changed standards may require adaptation; context decides whether the change was unfair.
brief.boundaryZh: 需指出前後要求，不因改變便斷定有人欺騙，也不把舊成果說成毫無價值。
brief.misconceptionZh: 判準改變不等於目前已符合新標準，仍需核對差距。
brief.outcomeZh: 能比較前後要求，提出與新判準相關的下一步。

options.en: Entries now need development notes as well as a finished image.
options.zh: 投稿現在除完成圖外，還需發展筆記。

options.en: The organisers no longer want a finished image.
options.zh: 主辦方不再需要完成圖。

options.en: The new requirement applies only after the entries have been judged.
options.zh: 新要求只在投稿評審後才適用。

options.en: Development notes were required in exactly the same way last year.
options.zh: 去年已以完全相同方式要求發展筆記。

listening.explanationZh: used to與this year建立前後比較；also表示新增，而非取代完成圖。
listening.en: The goalposts have moved for our exhibition entries: a finished image used to be enough, but this year the organisers also want notes showing how the idea developed.
listening.zh: 展覽投稿的要求改變了：以前只交完成圖便足夠，今年主辦方還要說明構思發展的筆記。

reply.promptEn: Why are you adding development notes to the exhibition entry?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼在展覽投稿加上發展筆記？

options.en: This year the organisers want to see the process as well as the finished image.
options.zh: 今年主辦方想看過程，也想看完成圖。

options.en: The goalposts have moved, and the entry now needs evidence of how the idea developed.
options.zh: 要求改變了，現在投稿需交代構思發展的依據。

options.en: The previous image-only submission would not meet the new requirements.
options.zh: 以前只交圖的做法，不符合新要求。

options.en: I need to show the development because the submission criteria have changed.
options.zh: 投稿判準改了，所以我需展示發展過程。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以新增過程要求解釋工作，不自行指控主辦方不公。

scene.promptZh: 讀書會以前只要各人推薦一本書，這期還要回應另一人的推薦。你已選書，但尚未寫回應。哪句準確？

options.en: The goalposts have moved; I still need to respond to someone else’s recommendation.
options.zh: 要求改了；我仍需回應別人的推薦。

options.en: Choosing my book means I have already met both current requirements.
options.zh: 選好書表示我已符合目前兩項要求。

options.en: The group has dropped book recommendations in favour of responses only.
options.zh: 小組已取消推薦書，只保留回應。

scene.explanationZh: 新增回應工作仍待完成，原本推薦也仍需要。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 the goalposts have moved 推出？

options.en: Expectations differ from those previously used.
options.zh: 期望與以前所用的不同。

options.en: A particular person deliberately acted unfairly.
options.zh: 某個人故意作出不公平行為。

options.en: Someone may need to check what the new criteria require.
options.zh: 有人可能需核對新判準要求甚麼。

contrast.explanationZh: 要求變了，不等於已知誰改、為何改或是否不公。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說以前交圖便夠，今年也不用看投稿通知；通知明寫另需發展筆記。哪句回應最好？

options.en: The goalposts have moved, so let us check what process notes we need alongside the image.
options.zh: 要求改了，所以一起核對完成圖以外需哪些過程筆記吧。

options.en: We can submit the image alone because it met the previous criteria.
options.zh: 只交圖便可，因它符合以前的判準。

options.en: We should send only the notes because the image has been replaced by the new requirement.
options.zh: 只交筆記便可，因新增要求已取代完成圖。

dialogue.explanationZh: 按現行通知保留兩部分，不沿用舊要求，也不把新增當取代。

speaking.en: The goalposts have moved, so I want to compare the new requirements with the work we have already done.
speaking.zh: 要求改了，所以我想把新要求與已完成工作作比較。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再連結要求改變及實際核對。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：地方志項目以前接受匿名照片，現在刊登前需確認署名及分享許可。你想暫緩未能聯絡拍攝者的照片，保留其他已核對的資料。用一至兩句英文說明。

examples.en: The goalposts have moved: we now need credits and permission before publishing these photographs. I will hold back the unverified images while keeping the checked material ready.
examples.zh: 要求改了：刊登照片前，現在需有署名及許可；我會暫緩未核實圖像，同時保留已核對資料以備使用。

examples.en: Since the goalposts have moved, the old anonymous-photo list is not enough for publication. We should contact the photographers before including those images.
examples.zh: 要求已改，以前的匿名照片清單不足以供刊登；納入那些圖像前，應先聯絡拍攝者。

writing.selfCheckZh: 清楚指出新署名許可要求，以暫緩和聯絡回應；保留其他已核對資料，不把所有工作當作廢。

takeaways.en: The goalposts had moved by the next round, when teams also had to explain their testing method.
takeaways.zh: 到下一輪，要求已改，隊伍還需解釋測試方法。

takeaways.en: The goalposts have moved for the award, so the committee is publishing a fresh checklist.
takeaways.zh: 獎項要求已改，所以委員會正發布新清單。

lessons.titleZh: 把資料灌進學生腦袋

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Good teaching is more than filling students' heads.

brief.meaningEn: Present learners as containers receiving information, often to contrast memorisation with deeper understanding or use.
brief.meaningZh: 把學習者比作接收資料的容器，常用以對照記憶與深入理解或應用。
brief.grammar: fill students’ heads with + information; fill their/our heads; identify what is supplied and whether learners can use it.
brief.register: Creative container metaphor in an educational argument. It can be critical, but remembering facts is not inherently useless.
brief.boundaryZh: 不能因批評只灌輸便說記憶全無價值；需分清接收資料與能否運用。
brief.misconceptionZh: 這不是人頭的實際填充，也不代表學生沒有思考能力。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述資訊輸入的限制，提出檢驗理解或應用的具體任務。

options.en: Remembering dates had not yet led to explaining connections between events.
options.zh: 記住日期尚未令他們能解釋事件間的關係。

options.en: The students had not received any dates in the lesson.
options.zh: 學生在課堂沒接收任何日期。

options.en: The discussion showed that they could already explain the links clearly.
options.zh: 討論顯示，他們早已能清楚解釋關係。

options.en: The timeline task asked them to replace the dates with unrelated stories.
options.zh: 時間線任務要求以無關故事取代日期。

listening.explanationZh: 日期已記住，但關係未解釋清楚；附理由時間線要把知識連起來。
listening.en: The lesson filled students’ heads with dates, but the follow-up discussion showed they could not yet explain why the events were connected; the teacher asked them to build a timeline with reasons.
listening.zh: 課堂把日期灌進學生腦袋，但之後討論顯示，他們仍未能解釋事件為何相連；老師請他們製作附理由的時間線。

reply.promptEn: Why did the teacher ask for reasons on the timeline?
reply.promptZh: 老師為甚麼要求在時間線加上理由？

options.en: The students needed to show how the events were connected.
options.zh: 學生需展示事件如何相連。

options.en: Filling students’ heads with dates had not yet helped them explain the links.
options.zh: 把日期灌進學生腦袋，仍未幫他們解釋關係。

options.en: Recalling the dates was not enough to demonstrate understanding of the sequence.
options.zh: 回想日期不足以展示對事件脈絡的理解。

options.en: The discussion revealed a gap between remembering information and explaining it.
options.zh: 討論顯示，記住資料與解釋資料之間仍有差距。

reply.explanationZh: 四句回應需要理由的原因，不把事實記憶一概否定。

scene.promptZh: 新導賞員背得出展品名稱，卻未能用例子解答訪客的材料問題。培訓者想補練解說，而非刪去基本資料。哪句貼切？

options.en: We have filled their heads with names; now they need practice explaining how the objects were made.
options.zh: 我們已把名稱灌進他們腦袋；現在需練習解釋物件如何製成。

options.en: They can already answer the material questions, so no explanation practice is needed.
options.zh: 他們早已能答材料問題，所以不需練解說。

options.en: The names should be removed from the training because basic information has no use.
options.zh: 基本資料沒用途，所以培訓應刪去名稱。

scene.explanationZh: 保留名稱的基礎作用，增加具體材料解說練習。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 filling students’ heads 的批評推出？

options.en: Receiving information may need to be followed by opportunities to use it.
options.zh: 接收資料後，可能需有運用機會。

options.en: Remembering any factual information is always pointless.
options.zh: 記住任何事實資料都必定毫無意義。

options.en: The speaker may be criticising a lesson limited to information delivery.
options.zh: 說話者可能批評只限於傳遞資料的課堂。

contrast.explanationZh: 批評只灌輸，並不等於否定所有事實記憶。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把歷史課改成完全不教日期，因為學生未能解釋事件關係。你想兼顧資料與理解。哪句最好？

options.en: Rather than only filling students’ heads with dates, let us help them use those dates to explain the links.
options.zh: 與其只把日期灌進學生腦袋，不如幫他們用日期解釋關係。

options.en: We should remove the dates and judge understanding only by how confidently they speak.
options.zh: 我們應刪去日期，只按說話是否自信判斷理解。

options.en: We can repeat the same date list and leave the connection questions until after the course.
options.zh: 我們可重複同一日期清單，把關係問題留待課程完結後。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把資料用於解釋，不以自信取代依據，也不延後應用練習。

speaking.en: We were filling their heads with terms, so we added a task that asked them to use the ideas in a new example.
speaking.zh: 我們一直把術語灌進他們腦袋，所以加了一項要在新例子運用概念的任務。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再連結資料與應用。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：課程將完，你記住了不少有用術語，但做項目時仍難比較例子。你想向導師寫溫和回饋，承認已學詞彙，並請在下一項目前一起做一次有步驟的比較示範，不貶低整門課。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The course filled our heads with useful terms, but I would have benefited from a worked comparison before the next project. Could we include one in the next session?
examples.zh: 課程把有用術語灌進我們腦袋，但下一項目前若有一次有步驟的比較，我會更受益；下次可否加入？

examples.en: Filling our heads with terms helped me recognise the vocabulary; could we also work through a comparison before starting the next project?
examples.zh: 把術語灌進腦袋，幫我認得詞彙；開始下一項目前，可否也一起逐步做一次比較？

writing.selfCheckZh: 以學習者身份承認詞彙收穫及仍欠比較應用，提出有禮而具體的後續請求，不把回饋寫成否定整門課。

takeaways.en: The course filled our heads with labels before we had a chance to compare the actual objects.
takeaways.zh: 課程在我們有機會比較實物前，先把標籤灌進腦袋。

takeaways.en: They had filled students’ heads with facts, then realised the project needed questions that connected those facts.
takeaways.zh: 他們把事實灌進學生腦袋後，才發現項目需有把事實連起來的問題。

lessons.titleZh: 只有單向付出的關係

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Learning should not be a one-way street.

brief.meaningEn: A relationship or process in which information, effort or benefit moves only one way.
brief.meaningZh: 資料、付出或好處只向一方流動的關係或過程。
brief.grammar: be a one-way street; often not/should not be a one-way street; explain what should move in both directions.
brief.register: Established road metaphor; two-way participation need not mean identical roles or equal speaking time.
brief.boundaryZh: 需指出哪一方只接收或付出；互動不等於每人工作完全一樣。
brief.misconceptionZh: 反對單向過程可要求有回應渠道，不表示主持者不應解說。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出具體的回饋或互相支持安排。

options.en: Instructions went out without a way for volunteers to send back problems before decisions.
options.zh: 指示發出去，但義工不能在決定前回報問題。

options.en: Volunteers decided the schedule before the coordinator gave any information.
options.zh: 義工在統籌者提供資料前，已決定時間表。

options.en: The meetings already included a problem-reporting round before the schedule was fixed.
options.zh: 時間表定案前，會議已有報告問題的環節。

options.en: The coordinator had stopped sending instructions and only received questions.
options.zh: 統籌者已停止發指示，只接收問題。

listening.explanationZh: 只發指示、沒有決定前回報渠道，才是這裏的單向問題。
listening.en: The planning meetings had become a one-way street: the coordinator sent instructions, but the volunteers had no way to report problems before the schedule was fixed.
listening.zh: 規劃會議已變成單向過程：統籌者發指示，但時間表定案前，義工沒有渠道報告問題。

reply.promptEn: Why did the volunteers want a change to the meetings?
reply.promptZh: 義工為甚麼想改變會議方式？

options.en: They needed a way to report practical problems before the schedule was settled.
options.zh: 他們需要在時間表定案前，報告實際問題的渠道。

options.en: The meetings had become a one-way street, with instructions but no route for their feedback.
options.zh: 會議變成單向過程，有指示卻沒有他們回饋的渠道。

options.en: The coordinator was not hearing the difficulties behind the proposed timetable.
options.zh: 統籌者沒有聽到擬定時間表背後的困難。

options.en: They wanted their experience to inform the plan rather than only receiving orders.
options.zh: 他們想用經驗幫助規劃，而不只接收命令。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都要求在規劃前讓實際困難有回應渠道，不取代統籌者角色。

scene.promptZh: 朋友總找你核對申請信，卻在你求同類幫助時一概不回覆。你想討論互相支持。哪句準確？

options.en: The support has become a one-way street, and I would like us to discuss what we can offer each other.
options.zh: 支援變成單向付出，我想討論大家可互相提供甚麼。

options.en: We have already agreed a balanced way to help each other.
options.zh: 我們已議定均衡的互助方法。

options.en: The problem is that neither of us has ever asked for help.
options.zh: 問題是我們兩人都從未求助。

scene.explanationZh: 已有一方多次求助、另一方同類求助不獲回應；適合談互相支持。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 not a one-way street 推出？

options.en: There should be some meaningful exchange.
options.zh: 應有某種有意義的交流。

options.en: Both sides must perform identical tasks for exactly the same time.
options.zh: 雙方必須做完全相同的工作，花完全相同的時間。

options.en: Different roles can still allow responses in both directions.
options.zh: 不同角色仍可容許雙向回應。

contrast.explanationZh: 雙向說有回應與交流，不必把角色及時間配成一模一樣。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說只要統籌者講得更久便能解決單向問題，但義工仍不能回報困難。哪句最好？

options.en: A longer briefing would still be a one-way street unless volunteers can raise the problems that affect the plan.
options.zh: 除非義工可提出影響計劃的問題，否則簡報更長仍是單向過程。

options.en: We should extend the instructions and leave the reporting channel unchanged.
options.zh: 我們應延長指示講解，維持原來的回報渠道。

options.en: We should hear about problems only after the schedule is fixed, with no time left for revision.
options.zh: 我們應待時間表定案、已無時間修訂後，才聽取問題。

dialogue.explanationZh: 關鍵是相關問題能回到規劃中，不是講更久或換成無關交流。

speaking.en: The discussion should not be a one-way street; we need a way to hear how the plan works for the people using it.
speaking.zh: 討論不應是單向過程；我們需有渠道聽取使用者怎樣看計劃實行情況。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再提出實際回應渠道。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小型刊物向讀者徵集街道回憶，但一直沒有回告故事怎被選用。你想在新一期加入「讀者來信回應」欄，解釋編輯取捨，也邀讀者更正。用一至兩句英文提出安排。

examples.en: Collecting memories should not be a one-way street. A letters column could explain our editorial choices and invite readers to correct the details.
examples.zh: 徵集回憶不應是單向過程；來信欄可解釋編輯取捨，並邀讀者更正細節。

examples.en: The magazine can avoid becoming a one-way street by responding to contributors and showing how their stories were used. We should also welcome corrections.
examples.zh: 刊物可透過回覆投稿者、交代故事用途，避免變成單向過程；我們也應歡迎更正。

writing.selfCheckZh: 提出編輯回告及讀者更正兩種互動，不只再次徵集，也不承諾所有稿件必刊。

takeaways.en: The partnership became a one-way street when only one group supplied equipment and received no support in return.
takeaways.zh: 合作只由一組提供器材而得不到回助時，變成了單向付出。

takeaways.en: Our interviews should not be a one-way street; participants need to know how their contributions will be used.
takeaways.zh: 訪談不應是單向過程；參與者需知道他們的貢獻將如何使用。

lessons.titleZh: 被視為唯一重要的事

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Grades are not the be-all and end-all of education.

brief.meaningEn: The thing treated as the most important or the sole purpose of an activity.
brief.meaningZh: 被當成最重要的事，或某活動的唯一目的。
brief.grammar: be the be-all and end-all of + activity; often not the be-all and end-all; identify the other relevant values.
brief.register: Established emphatic idiom, commonly used to reject an excessively narrow priority.
brief.boundaryZh: 不是唯一重要，不等於毫無重要；需保留相關因素的實際作用。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不要把反對單一尺度改成反對評估本身。
brief.outcomeZh: 能承認一項指標用途，也說明其他需要。

options.en: It matters alongside learning and cooperation.
options.zh: 它重要，同時也重視學習與合作。

options.en: It is the only purpose of the play.
options.zh: 它是校劇的唯一目的。

options.en: It is irrelevant to planning the performance.
options.zh: 它與演出規劃無關。

options.en: It measures how much rehearsal support each performer received.
options.zh: 它能量度每位演出者得到多少排練支援。

listening.explanationZh: matter承認售票重要，not the be-all and end-all保留其他教育及合作目的。
listening.en: Ticket sales matter, but they are not the be-all and end-all of our school play; we also want first-time performers to learn how to rehearse and support one another.
listening.zh: 售票數重要，但不是校劇唯一重要的事；我們也想讓首次演出者學習排練及互相支持。

reply.promptEn: Why are you reviewing rehearsal support as well as ticket sales?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼除了售票數，也檢討排練支援？

options.en: The performers’ learning is another important purpose of the play.
options.zh: 演出者學習也是校劇的重要目的。

options.en: Ticket sales are not the be-all and end-all; learning and cooperation matter too.
options.zh: 售票數不是唯一重要的事，學習及合作也重要。

options.en: The sales figures do not tell us how the new performers were supported.
options.zh: 售票數字不能告訴我們新人獲得怎樣的支援。

options.en: We want to judge the experience by more than its income alone.
options.zh: 我們想評估這次經驗，不只看收入。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給出票房以外的相關目的，同時不否定收入作用。

scene.promptZh: 你選義工項目，交通方便是考慮之一，但也需看工作是否適合及能否守時。哪句準確？

options.en: Convenience is not the be-all and end-all; the role and schedule also need to fit.
options.zh: 方便不是唯一重要的事，工作及時間也需適合。

options.en: The easiest journey settles the choice before we check the role.
options.zh: 未查工作內容前，最方便路程便決定選擇。

options.en: Travel time should be excluded from the decision completely.
options.zh: 應完全不把交通時間納入決定。

scene.explanationZh: 交通有用但非唯一尺度，工作內容及時間也相關。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 not the be-all and end-all？

options.en: A factor can be important without being the sole priority.
options.zh: 一項因素可重要，卻非唯一優先事項。

options.en: The factor has no relevance and should be ignored.
options.zh: 該因素完全無關，應被忽略。

options.en: Other purposes should also enter the discussion.
options.zh: 討論也應包括其他目的。

contrast.explanationZh: 不是全部，不等於完全無關。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴聽到票房不是唯一目的，就想刪去售票紀錄；你仍需核對收支。哪句最好？

options.en: Sales are not the be-all and end-all, but we still need the records alongside our review of learning.
options.zh: 售票數不是唯一重要的事，但檢討學習之餘，仍需保留紀錄。

options.en: We can remove the sales records because another purpose has been identified.
options.zh: 既然找到另一目的，便可刪去售票紀錄。

options.en: We should use the sales total as our only evidence about rehearsal quality.
options.zh: 我們應只用售票總數，判斷排練質素。

dialogue.explanationZh: 並列相關評估，既不刪必要記錄，也不把票房代替所有學習證據。

speaking.en: Speed is not the be-all and end-all of this task; the information also needs to be accurate and useful.
speaking.zh: 速度不是這項任務唯一重要的事；資料也需準確及有用。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把一項尺度放回多個目的。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：小組設計社區地圖，有人只比較印刷價錢。你想在採購回覆中保留預算考慮，同時要求看清字體及折疊後是否易用的樣本。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: Price is not the be-all and end-all of the map order. Please send a sample so we can check the lettering and how easily the map folds.
examples.zh: 地圖訂單不只看價錢；請提供樣本，讓我們核對字體及地圖是否易摺。

examples.en: The budget matters, but price should not be the be-all and end-all. We also need a readable map that people can unfold and use easily.
examples.zh: 預算重要，但價錢不應是唯一重要的事；我們也需一份字體清楚、容易展開使用的地圖。

writing.selfCheckZh: 保留預算，另以樣本檢查可讀及摺疊使用，不把價錢低直接當整體最好。

takeaways.en: The final score was not the be-all and end-all of the practice match; we also reviewed how the players communicated.
takeaways.zh: 練習賽的最終比數不是唯一重要的事；我們也檢討球員如何溝通。

takeaways.en: For this archive, a large collection is not the be-all and end-all if readers cannot locate the records.
takeaways.zh: 對這檔案庫來說，收藏多不是唯一重要的事；讀者也需能找到記錄。

lessons.titleZh: 把人或事過分理想化

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: These subjects were put on a pedestal at school.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.expression: puts another person on too high a pedestal
sources.sentence: A fan puts another person on too high a pedestal.
sources.locatorNote: PDF page240, table1, row4; exact guide source retained.

brief.meaningEn: Admire someone or something so much that faults or limitations receive too little attention.
brief.meaningZh: 過分推崇某人或事，以致忽略缺點或限制。
brief.grammar: put someone/something on a pedestal; put in past; putting; on too high a pedestal adds degree. Place the object before on.
brief.register: Established idealisation idiom; praise alone is not necessarily putting someone on a pedestal.
brief.boundaryZh: 需有過度推崇或忽略限制的依據，不把一切敬佩說成錯。
brief.misconceptionZh: 保持尊重仍可查核或提出問題；理想化也不表示對方有特定壞行為。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分欣賞具體貢獻與把對象看成不應受檢視。

options.en: Admiration led the group to accept advice without considering its fit.
options.zh: 敬佩令小組不考慮是否合用便接受建議。

options.en: The group rejected the author’s advice before hearing any of it.
options.zh: 小組未聽作家意見便已拒絕。

options.en: The author had asked the group to copy her own characters.
options.zh: 作家曾要求小組抄她的角色。

options.en: The group checked each suggestion and retained only those that suited its story.
options.zh: 小組逐項核對，只保留適合故事的建議。

listening.explanationZh: 重點是未經判斷便接受，不是已知作家要求抄角色或建議全無用。
listening.en: We had put the visiting author on a pedestal and accepted every suggestion without checking whether it suited our story; her useful advice deserved attention, but our own characters still needed a consistent voice.
listening.zh: 我們過分推崇到訪作家，沒查建議是否適合故事便全接受；她有用的意見值得重視，但我們的角色仍需一致聲音。

reply.promptEn: Why do you want to review the author’s suggestions before making changes?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼想先檢視作家建議，再改作品？

options.en: We should check which ideas fit our own characters.
options.zh: 我們應查哪些構思適合自己的角色。

options.en: We put her on a pedestal and stopped considering whether each suggestion suited the story.
options.zh: 我們過分推崇她，不再考慮各建議是否適合故事。

options.en: Admiring her work does not settle how we should revise ours.
options.zh: 欣賞她的作品，不能替我們決定如何修改自己的作品。

options.en: Her advice may help, but we still need to consider our story’s needs.
options.zh: 她的建議可能有幫助，但我們仍需考慮故事需要。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提出恢復判斷的理由，不把作家批成沒有貢獻。

scene.promptZh: 學會因前會長曾辦成功活動，便不再核對他新方案的場地及預算。你想承認過往貢獻，也提醒評估。哪句貼切？

options.en: We should not put him on a pedestal; his new plan still needs a venue and budget check.
options.zh: 我們不應把他過分理想化；他的新方案仍需核對場地及預算。

options.en: The old event’s budget has already been adopted for this new plan.
options.zh: 舊活動的預算已被採用於這個新方案。

options.en: We should reject the new plan solely because he led the earlier event.
options.zh: 只因他帶領過上次活動，我們就應拒絕新方案。

scene.explanationZh: 尊重經驗與核對新方案可並存，過往成功不補足缺少數據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 put someone on a pedestal？

options.en: Refusing to examine an admired person’s advice because it must be right.
options.zh: 認為敬佩者的意見必定正確，因而拒絕檢視。

options.en: Praising a specific contribution while still checking the new proposal.
options.zh: 稱讚具體貢獻，同時仍核對新提案。

options.en: Treating the person as above the criticism applied to others.
options.zh: 把該人視為應免受其他人同樣會接受的批評。

contrast.explanationZh: 具體欣賞加正常核對，並非過度理想化。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友以為不再過分推崇作家，就應把她建議全部刪去；其中有幾項可能有用。哪句最好？

options.en: We need not put her on a pedestal or dismiss her advice; let us test what fits the story.
options.zh: 我們不需過分理想化她，也不需排斥她的意見；一起試哪些適合故事吧。

options.en: Her suggestions should be set aside because the characters belong to us.
options.zh: 角色屬於我們，所以她的建議應被擱置。

options.en: We can accept the next revision without reading it because she wrote it.
options.zh: 既然下一個修訂由她寫，便可未讀先接受。

dialogue.explanationZh: 獨立判斷並不等於刻意刪去有用意見，也不回到盲目接受。

speaking.en: I had put the speaker on a pedestal, so I needed to separate my admiration from the evidence for the proposal.
speaking.zh: 我曾把講者過分理想化，所以需把敬佩與支持提案的依據分開。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再區分敬佩與判斷。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你寫人物專訪，初稿只列老師獎項，忽略她願意談的失敗與修正。她希望文章呈現學習過程；你要向編輯解釋怎樣修改，不捏造缺點。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: My draft put her on a pedestal by listing only the awards. I will include her own account of the failed project and what she changed afterwards.
examples.zh: 初稿只列獎項，把她過分理想化；我會加入她親述的失敗項目及之後的修正。

examples.en: Rather than put the teacher on a pedestal, the profile can show how she learned from a setback. We should use the experiences she has agreed to discuss.
examples.zh: 人物稿不必把老師過分理想化，可展示她如何從挫折學習；我們應使用她已同意談的經歷。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以獲同意的真實經歷補足人物學習過程，不為了平衡而捏造缺點或削去成就。

takeaways.en: The committee put the old design on a pedestal and stopped checking whether it served new readers.
takeaways.zh: 委員會過分推崇舊設計，不再核對它是否適合新讀者。

takeaways.en: She admired her mentor without putting him on a pedestal; they could still discuss where an idea needed work.
takeaways.zh: 她欣賞導師，卻不把他過分理想化；他們仍可討論構思哪裏需改善。

lessons.titleZh: 被當作次要配角的活動

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Clubs are not merely side dishes in school life.

brief.meaningEn: Activities or elements portrayed as secondary additions rather than central parts of something.
brief.meaningZh: 把活動或元素比作次要附加項目，而非主要部分。
brief.grammar: Treat/view activities as side dishes; often not merely side dishes. State the larger activity to which the image relates.
brief.register: Creative food metaphor in the source; real side dishes remain literal in a meal context.
brief.boundaryZh: 比喻關乎地位與作用，不直接決定時間、預算或所有人的喜好。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是次要不等於必須取代其他主要工作。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以具體貢獻解釋活動的核心作用，而不只爭取多些時間。

options.en: The clubs’ learning role versus treating them as secondary extras.
options.zh: 學會的學習作用，與把它們當次要附加活動的看法。

options.en: The types of food served after rehearsal.
options.zh: 排練後供應的食物種類。

options.en: A decision to replace every classroom lesson with drama.
options.zh: 以戲劇取代每節課堂的決定。

options.en: A claim that the club had no effect on cooperation.
options.zh: 學會對合作沒有影響的主張。

listening.explanationZh: 具體學習作用支持不只附加活動，沒有把排練當食物或說要取代所有課堂。
listening.en: The school no longer treated drama and music clubs as side dishes added after the serious learning: students used rehearsals to practise listening, revising ideas and working with different partners.
listening.zh: 學校不再把戲劇及音樂學會當作「正經學習」後的次要配菜；學生透過排練練習聆聽、修訂想法及與不同伙伴合作。

reply.promptEn: Why does the school value these clubs as part of learning?
reply.promptZh: 學校為甚麼把這些學會視為學習的一部分？

options.en: Rehearsals give students practice in listening and revising ideas.
options.zh: 排練讓學生練習聆聽及修訂想法。

options.en: They are not merely side dishes; the clubs develop skills used with different partners.
options.zh: 它們不只是次要配菜；學會培養與不同伙伴合作時運用的技能。

options.en: The activity contributes to learning rather than only filling time after lessons.
options.zh: 活動有助學習，不只填滿課後時間。

options.en: Students learn through the shared work of rehearsing together.
options.zh: 學生透過共同排練的工作學習。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以具體學習作用說明重要性，不以參加人數代替作用證據。

scene.promptZh: 社區調查把翻譯安排當可有可無，但已有居民說沒有譯文便無法回答。你想解釋其參與作用。哪句合適？

options.en: Translations are not side dishes here; they make participation possible for these residents.
options.zh: 翻譯在這裏不是次要配菜；它讓這些居民能參與。

options.en: The translated version only changes how the page looks to readers.
options.zh: 譯本只改變讀者看到的版面外觀。

options.en: The residents have already answered the untranslated version without difficulty.
options.zh: 居民已毫無困難地回答未翻譯版本。

scene.explanationZh: 居民已指出語言限制，所以翻譯關係到能否參與，不只是裝飾。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 not merely side dishes 推出？

options.en: An element has a substantive role in the larger activity.
options.zh: 某元素在整項活動中有實質作用。

options.en: It must replace the other main elements entirely.
options.zh: 它必須完全取代其他主要元素。

options.en: The speaker rejects treating it as an optional minor addition.
options.zh: 說話者反對把它當可有可無的小附加項目。

contrast.explanationZh: 強調其作用，不代表它需排走其他工作。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說戲劇會有學習作用，就應取消其他課堂只排戲；你想保留互補。哪句最好？

options.en: The clubs are not merely side dishes, but their contribution can sit alongside other lessons rather than replace them.
options.zh: 學會不只是次要配菜，但它可與其他課堂互補，而非取代它們。

options.en: We should remove other lessons because rehearsal now counts as learning.
options.zh: 既然排練算學習，便應刪去其他課堂。

options.en: We can keep calling the club a spare-time extra without reviewing what students learn.
options.zh: 我們可不看學生學到甚麼，繼續把學會稱為空餘時間活動。

dialogue.explanationZh: 承認核心學習作用並保留互補，不把重視改成取代。

speaking.en: The interviews are not side dishes in this project; they shape the questions we ask about the records.
speaking.zh: 訪談在這項目不是次要配菜；它們影響我們向記錄提出的問題。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再指出比喻背後的實際作用。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你策劃展覽，想把訪客回應從出口處的小留言改為修訂解說的依據，並安排每周閱讀及回覆。用一至兩句英文向組員解釋，不承諾每條意見都照做。

examples.en: Visitor responses should not be side dishes added after the exhibition is finished. We can read them each week and use relevant comments to revise the explanations.
examples.zh: 訪客回應不應是展覽完成後才加的次要配菜；我們可每周閱讀，並用相關意見修訂解說。

examples.en: If we stop treating responses as side dishes, we need a routine for reading and answering them. Relevant suggestions can then inform the next version of the display.
examples.zh: 若不再把回應當次要配菜，便需有定期閱讀及回覆的安排；相關建議可幫助修訂下一版展示。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把訪客回應連到有負責及定期處理的修訂過程，不只是加留言箱，也不承諾照單全收。

takeaways.en: The editor refused to treat the maps as side dishes because readers needed them to follow the journeys.
takeaways.zh: 編輯不把地圖當次要配菜，因為讀者需靠它們理解旅程。

takeaways.en: Community interviews were not side dishes; they changed which events the team investigated.
takeaways.zh: 社區訪談不是次要配菜；它們改變團隊研究哪些事件。

lessons.titleZh: 構成核心內容的一部分

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Creative projects are part of the main course now.

brief.meaningEn: An element portrayed as belonging to the central substance of an activity, rather than as an optional extra.
brief.meaningZh: 把某元素比作活動核心內容的一部分，而非可有可無的附加項目。
brief.grammar: be/become part of the main course; name the larger activity. Food image is figurative outside a meal context.
brief.register: Creative main-course metaphor in the source; related to but not interchangeable in tone with an actual meal description.
brief.boundaryZh: 是核心一部分，不表示佔全部時間或其他元素都不重要。
brief.misconceptionZh: 核心地位需以作用支持，不能只因加了時間便假定學習有效。
brief.outcomeZh: 能解釋一項安排如何構成主要目的，並說明實際做法。

options.en: A central course activity that informs revision.
options.zh: 幫助修訂的核心課程活動。

options.en: An optional activity outside the course requirements.
options.zh: 課程要求以外的自選活動。

options.en: A replacement for making any prototype.
options.zh: 取代所有製作原型工作的活動。

options.en: A test completed only after the final version was fixed.
options.zh: 只在最終版本定案後才完成的測試。

listening.explanationZh: 觀察連到修訂，並明說不再自選；沒有取代製作或等到定稿後才試。
listening.en: In our design course, testing with users became part of the main course: each team revised a prototype after observing where visitors hesitated, rather than leaving the test as an optional extra.
listening.zh: 在設計課中，使用者測試成為核心內容的一部分；各隊觀察訪客在哪裏猶豫後修訂原型，不再把測試當自選附加活動。

reply.promptEn: Why must each team include a user test before revising the prototype?
reply.promptZh: 每隊為甚麼都需先做使用者測試，再修原型？

options.en: The course uses observed visitor difficulties to guide revision.
options.zh: 課程以觀察到的訪客困難，引導修訂。

options.en: Testing is part of the main course now, not an optional activity after the design work.
options.zh: 測試現在是核心內容的一部分，不是設計工作後的自選活動。

options.en: The test is built into the process of developing the design.
options.zh: 測試已納入發展設計的過程。

options.en: Each team needs practical evidence before deciding what to change.
options.zh: 每隊決定改甚麼前，都需有實際依據。

reply.explanationZh: 四句解釋測試的核心作用，不把它說成只多一項無關要求。

scene.promptZh: 地方刊物以人物故事為主，現決定每篇都附資料來源，讓讀者能追查。哪句準確？

options.en: Source notes are part of the main course, not a decorative addition to these stories.
options.zh: 來源說明是這些故事核心內容的一部分，不是裝飾性附加項目。

options.en: The notes replace the stories, so no narrative will be printed.
options.zh: 說明取代故事，所以不會刊登敘事。

options.en: Readers will receive source notes only if there is unused space.
options.zh: 只有剩餘版位時，讀者才會看到來源說明。

scene.explanationZh: 每篇附來源以便追查，表明它屬主要內容，而非剩位才加。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 part of the main course 推出？

options.en: An element contributes to the core activity.
options.zh: 某元素有助核心活動。

options.en: The element must occupy the entire programme.
options.zh: 該元素必須佔整個活動。

options.en: The speaker does not view it as merely an optional extra.
options.zh: 說話者不把它只視為自選附加項目。

contrast.explanationZh: 一部分仍非全部；核心地位不自行決定佔時。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把設計課測試放到定稿後自願參加，但各隊需靠結果修原型。哪句最好？

options.en: Testing is part of the main course because it informs revision, so it belongs before the final design is fixed.
options.zh: 測試因有助修訂而屬核心內容，所以應在設計定稿前進行。

options.en: We can move the test after publication and keep the same revision deadline.
options.zh: 我們可把測試移到發布後，仍維持原來修訂期限。

options.en: We can use only the team’s impressions instead of observing visitors with the prototype.
options.zh: 我們可只用團隊印象，代替觀察訪客使用原型。

dialogue.explanationZh: 測試需在可用結果修訂的時段，並觀察實際訪客；不能等發布後才試，也不能只以團隊印象代替。

speaking.en: Reflection is part of the main course in our project because it changes what we try in the next round.
speaking.zh: 反思是我們項目核心內容的一部分，因為它會改變下一輪嘗試。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再以作用解釋核心地位。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：讀書會改用雙人主持，每次其中一人帶討論，另一人整理未答問題，供下次選書參考。你要寫主持指引，把跟進問題列為正式工作，而非散場後有空才做。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: Following up unanswered questions is part of the main course for our reading group. The second host should record them so they can inform the next book choice.
examples.zh: 跟進未答問題是讀書會核心工作的一部分；第二位主持應記下問題，供下次選書參考。

examples.en: The question record is part of the main course, not something to do only if time remains after the meeting. It will help both hosts plan what the group reads next.
examples.zh: 問題記錄屬核心工作，不是會後剩時間才做；它會幫兩位主持規劃小組下一步讀甚麼。

glossary.en: plan what the group reads next
glossary.zh: 規劃小組下一步讀甚麼

writing.selfCheckZh: 把整理問題列為有角色及後續用途的正式工作，並保留帶討論的另一位主持。

takeaways.en: Listening to residents became part of the main course when their concerns shaped the exhibition plan.
takeaways.zh: 居民關注影響展覽計劃後，聽取居民意見成為核心內容的一部分。

takeaways.en: The draft review is part of the main course, so the timetable leaves room to act on it.
takeaways.zh: 草稿審閱屬核心內容，所以時間表留有按意見修訂的空間。

lessons.titleEn: a museum piece to be admired behind glass
lessons.titleZh: 只供欣賞卻沒有實際運用的陳列品

target.pattern: \ba museum piece to be admired behind glass\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A living language is not a museum piece to be admired behind glass.
sources.expression: a museum piece to be admired behind glass

brief.meaningEn: Something portrayed as a static object for admiration rather than something actively used or developed.
brief.meaningZh: 把事物比作只供欣賞的靜態陳列品，而非可實際運用或發展的東西。
brief.grammar: Treat something as a museum piece to be admired behind glass; often reject this treatment. Explain the actual practice being contrasted.
brief.register: An extended creative comparison in the source, not a fixed rule about museums or an attack on preserving historic objects.
brief.boundaryZh: 比喻反對只觀賞不用，不是否定觀察、歷史研究或文物保存。
brief.misconceptionZh: 要指出何種實際用途被忽略，不把一切欣賞說成錯。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用完整比喻對比靜態欣賞與有目的的運用。

options.en: Learning its history and using it for real exchanges.
options.zh: 學習它的歷史，同時用它作實際交流。

options.en: Studying history while avoiding all conversation practice.
options.zh: 研究歷史，同時避開所有對話練習。

options.en: Replacing historical study with information about museum buildings.
options.zh: 以博物館建築資料取代歷史學習。

options.en: Preserving the language by restricting it to written display labels.
options.zh: 把語言限制在文字展覽標示，以作保存。

listening.explanationZh: do both承認歷史及實際交流；陳列品是只看不用的延伸比喻。
listening.en: If we treat the language as a museum piece to be admired behind glass, we may learn about its history without using it to ask questions or exchange ideas; our club wants to do both.
listening.zh: 若把語言當成隔着玻璃欣賞的博物館陳列品，我們可能只學其歷史，卻不用它提問或交流；我們的學會想兩者兼顧。

reply.promptEn: Why does the club include conversation as well as language history?
reply.promptZh: 學會為甚麼除了語言歷史，也安排對話？

options.en: We want to use what we learn to ask questions and exchange ideas.
options.zh: 我們想用所學來提問及交流想法。

options.en: We do not want the language to become a museum piece to be admired behind glass.
options.zh: 我們不想語言變成只隔着玻璃欣賞的博物館陳列品。

options.en: Historical knowledge matters, but active use matters as well.
options.zh: 歷史知識重要，實際運用也重要。

options.en: The club aims to connect understanding of the past with present communication.
options.zh: 學會想把對過去的理解，連到現在的溝通。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都回應加入實際交流的目的，沒有否定歷史學習。

scene.promptZh: 老劇本研究小組已保存原稿，現在還想試讀對白，觀察今天聽眾怎理解；不是要改動原件。哪句貼切？

options.en: The script need not remain a museum piece to be admired behind glass; a reading can explore how it sounds today.
options.zh: 劇本不必只是隔着玻璃欣賞的陳列品；試讀可探索它今天聽來如何。

options.en: A reading requires us to overwrite the preserved original.
options.zh: 試讀要求我們塗改保存的原稿。

options.en: Keeping the original means the group has already tested how an audience understands the dialogue.
options.zh: 保存原稿表示小組已測試觀眾如何理解對白。

scene.explanationZh: 運用複本試讀與保留原件可並行；保存本身未提供觀眾理解的資料。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由這個陳列品比喻的批評推出？

options.en: Admiration alone may leave practical use unexplored.
options.zh: 只欣賞可能未探索實際用途。

options.en: Historical preservation has no value and should stop.
options.zh: 歷史保存毫無價值，應停止。

options.en: An activity can combine preservation with thoughtful use.
options.zh: 活動可兼顧保存及審慎運用。

contrast.explanationZh: 批評只欣賞不用，不等於反對保存。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說若語言不只是陳列品，就不用再學它的歷史；學會原定要兼顧交流及歷史。哪句最好？

options.en: We can avoid treating it as a museum piece to be admired behind glass while still learning its history through active discussion.
options.zh: 我們可透過實際討論學歷史，不把語言只當隔着玻璃欣賞的陳列品。

options.en: We should remove the history sessions because conversation has a practical use.
options.zh: 既然對話有實際用途，便應刪去歷史環節。

options.en: We can keep conversation out of the club and call reading the display notes active exchange.
options.zh: 我們可不安排對話，並把讀展示說明稱作實際交流。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把歷史內容用於討論，保留兩個目標，而非另立歷史與交流的二選一。

speaking.en: I do not want the tradition to become a museum piece to be admired behind glass; we can preserve its history and still explore how to use it.
speaking.zh: 我不想傳統變成只隔着玻璃欣賞的陳列品；我們可保留歷史，同時探索怎樣運用。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留保存與運用兩方面。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區保存了舊編織圖樣，打算用複印本辦工作坊，讓參加者試織並記下改用現有材料的結果；原件仍妥善收藏。你要向贊助者解釋活動目的。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: The pattern need not be a museum piece to be admired behind glass. Participants can try it from copies and record what happens with the materials available today.
examples.zh: 圖樣不必只是隔着玻璃欣賞的陳列品；參加者可用複本試織，記下使用今天可得材料的結果。

examples.en: We can preserve the original without treating the pattern as a museum piece to be admired behind glass. The workshop will let people practise the technique and document their adaptations.
examples.zh: 我們可保留原件，不把圖樣只當隔着玻璃欣賞的陳列品；工作坊會讓大家練習技法，並記錄調整。

writing.selfCheckZh: 解釋用複本學技法及記錄材料調整的目的，保留原件，不作破壞文物的推論。

takeaways.en: The old storytelling form need not be a museum piece to be admired behind glass; the group is trying it with new stories.
takeaways.zh: 舊說故事形式不必只是隔着玻璃欣賞的陳列品；小組正用新故事試這種形式。

takeaways.en: She refused to treat the recipe as a museum piece to be admired behind glass and recorded what she learned by cooking from a copy.
takeaways.zh: 她不把食譜只當隔着玻璃欣賞的陳列品，並記下用複本烹調所學。

english.evidence: Extended source comparison retained explicitly as creative. Different applications: language communication, script audience interpretation and craft adaptation documentation; all preserve original objects.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 突然沉默而不肯說話

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Nervous learners may clam up during a test.

brief.meaningEn: Suddenly become unwilling or unable to speak, often because of nerves or discomfort.
brief.meaningZh: 常因緊張或不自在，突然不肯或說不出話。
brief.grammar: clam up; clammed/clamming; intransitive; describe the situation without diagnosing an unspoken cause.
brief.register: Informal phrasal verb. Silence does not by itself prove ignorance, agreement or a particular motive.
brief.boundaryZh: 可形容突然不再說話，但原因需資料支持；不能把沉默當同意或能力差。
brief.misconceptionZh: 與預先選擇安靜聆聽不同，留意原本參與後突然停下的線索。
brief.outcomeZh: 能準確描述反應，並提出不施壓的溝通安排。

listening.promptZh: 甚麼改變及原因有直接依據？

options.en: She stopped speaking when recording began and later explained her worry.
options.zh: 開始錄音時她停止說話，之後親自解釋擔憂。

options.en: She remained equally talkative while the recorder was running.
options.zh: 錄音期間她仍一樣健談。

options.en: She said she could not recognise any of the photographs.
options.zh: 她說完全認不出照片。

options.en: She had requested silence before the informal discussion began.
options.zh: 非正式討論開始前，她已要求保持沉默。

listening.explanationZh: had been discussing與clammed up構成變化；擔憂來自她後來親述。
listening.en: Mira had been discussing the photographs freely, but she clammed up when the recorder was switched on; afterwards she said she had worried about a mistake being kept on tape.
listening.zh: 米拉原本自在地談照片，但錄音機一開便突然沉默；之後她說，擔心說錯的話會留在錄音裏。

reply.promptEn: Why did Mira stop talking when the recorder was switched on?
reply.promptZh: 錄音機開啟時，米拉為甚麼不再說話？

options.en: She later said she was worried about mistakes being kept on tape.
options.zh: 她後來說擔心錯話會留在錄音中。

options.en: She clammed up because she worried about a mistake being kept on tape.
options.zh: 她擔心說錯的話會留在錄音裏，所以突然沉默。

options.en: The possibility of a mistake remaining in the recording made her uncomfortable.
options.zh: 錯話可能留在錄音裏，令她不自在。

options.en: Her later explanation linked the silence to concern about being recorded.
options.zh: 她之後的解釋，把沉默與被錄下的擔憂連起來。

reply.explanationZh: 四句原因都有她親述支持，不猜成不懂照片或拒絕所有交流。

scene.promptZh: 故事角色本來在小組分享旅程，輪到公開發言卻突然說不出話；原因尚未問。哪句準確？

options.en: He clammed up when it was time to speak to the larger audience.
options.zh: 輪到向較大群觀眾發言時，他突然說不出話。

options.en: He calmly chose to listen throughout both discussions without speaking.
options.zh: 兩次討論他都平靜地選擇只聽不說。

options.en: He explained that he had never taken the journey he described.
options.zh: 他解釋自己從未走過剛才描述的旅程。

scene.explanationZh: 可描述突然沉默，卻不能代角色提供尚未問明的理由。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 someone clammed up 推出？

options.en: The person suddenly became silent.
options.zh: 那人突然沉默。

options.en: The person agreed with the proposal being discussed.
options.zh: 那人同意當時討論的提案。

options.en: More context may be needed to understand the silence.
options.zh: 可能需更多情境才能理解沉默。

contrast.explanationZh: 突然沉默不自行表示同意，原因及看法需再了解。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想繼續錄，說米拉不說話就是同意；她尚未給錄音許可。你怎回應？

options.en: She has clammed up, so let us pause and ask privately whether she wants to continue recording.
options.zh: 她突然沉默了，所以先暫停，私下問她是否想繼續錄音吧。

options.en: We can treat the silence as permission and keep recording.
options.zh: 我們可把沉默當許可，繼續錄音。

options.en: We should ask the next recorded question without addressing whether she wants the recorder on.
options.zh: 我們應繼續問下一條錄音問題，不處理她是否想開錄音機。

dialogue.explanationZh: 先釐清意願，不以沉默代許可，也不跳過當下限制。

speaking.en: He clammed up when the questions became personal, so I paused rather than assuming I knew why.
speaking.zh: 問題變得私人時，他突然沉默，所以我先暫停，而非以為已知原因。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再描述反應及審慎回應。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：朋友突然問你的家庭爭執，你當時沉默，現在想向他解釋不願即時談私人事，但願意分享自己接下來的安排。你要用第一身清楚界定可談範圍，不責怪提問者或替自己診斷。用一至兩句英文回覆。

examples.en: I clammed up when the question turned to the family disagreement because I did not want to discuss it then. I can tell you about my plans, but I would like to keep the private details to myself.
examples.zh: 問題轉到家人爭執時，我突然沉默，因為當時不想談；我可告訴你我的安排，但想保留私人細節。

examples.en: I clammed up at the unexpected personal question, and I would rather explain my next steps than discuss the argument. Could we keep our conversation to those plans for now?
examples.zh: 意料外的私人問題令我突然沉默；比起談爭執，我寧願解釋下一步；我們暫時只談那些安排，好嗎？

writing.selfCheckZh: 以第一身交代沉默及此刻不想談的界線，再提出願意分享的安排；不把沉默當同意，也不攻擊朋友或加診斷。

takeaways.en: I clammed up during the unexpected introduction, then asked if I could start again.
takeaways.zh: 突如其來的自我介紹時，我突然說不出話，之後問可否重來。

takeaways.en: She had been answering confidently before she clammed up at the question about home.
takeaways.zh: 談到家裏的問題令她突然沉默前，她一直自信地回答。

english.evidence: Final is first-person boundary-setting and a topic alternative after an unexpected personal question, distinct from narrator descriptions of larger-audience silence and recorded consent.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 理論可行卻受實際條件限制

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The plan works in theory but fails in small towns.

brief.meaningEn: Contrast what an idea suggests should work with what happens under actual conditions.
brief.meaningZh: 對照構想或理論上應可行的情況，與實際條件下發生的情況。
brief.grammar: In theory, clause, but clause; works in theory but...; the two parts need a meaningful contrast.
brief.register: Natural contrast frame, not a single indivisible idiom. A subject and verb may separate in theory and but.
brief.boundaryZh: 要列實際限制，不能只說理論不好；一次限制也不自動推成所有情況失敗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 理論上可行不等於已實際測試成功。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把預期與可觀察條件相對照，提出相關調整。

listening.promptZh: 預期與限制分別是甚麼？

options.en: Online booking could simplify the process, but some visitors still need another access route.
options.zh: 網上預約可簡化流程，但部分訪客仍需另一種使用渠道。

options.en: The telephone option has already been removed without affecting visitors.
options.zh: 電話選項已取消，且沒有影響訪客。

options.en: The online form has been tested successfully with every regular visitor.
options.zh: 網上表格已成功在每位常客身上測試。

options.en: The proposal was designed to make booking more complicated.
options.zh: 提案原本就是想令預約更複雜。

listening.explanationZh: 理論好處是簡化，實際限制是部分人連線不穩；仍需替代渠道。
listening.en: In theory, an online-only booking form would simplify the workshop, but several regular visitors have no reliable connection and still need a telephone option.
listening.zh: 理論上，只用網上預約表可簡化工作坊安排，但幾位常客連線不穩，仍需電話選項。

reply.promptEn: Why are you keeping the telephone option?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼保留電話選項？

options.en: Some regular visitors cannot rely on an internet connection.
options.zh: 部分常客不能依靠穩定網絡連線。

options.en: In theory, online-only booking is simpler, but it would leave some visitors without reliable access.
options.zh: 理論上只用網上預約較簡單，但會令部分訪客缺乏可靠使用渠道。

options.en: The proposed simplification does not meet everyone’s actual access needs.
options.zh: 所提簡化方法未能應付所有人的實際使用需要。

options.en: We need another route for people whose connection is unreliable.
options.zh: 我們需給連線不穩的人另一種渠道。

reply.explanationZh: 四句以已知使用需要作理由，不以一般喜好反對網上預約。

scene.promptZh: 排練表按連續兩小時安排，但場地租約中間有十五分鐘需清場；你想修正流程。哪句準確？

options.en: The timetable works in theory, but the required break interrupts the two-hour rehearsal.
options.zh: 時間表理論上可行，但必須的清場休息打斷兩小時排練。

options.en: The venue has already waived the required break.
options.zh: 場地已取消必須的休息。

options.en: The rehearsal was planned with that break included from the start.
options.zh: 排練最初已把那段休息計算在內。

scene.explanationZh: 列出原本連續安排與租約限制，才可作實際調整。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不符合 in theory...but... 的對照功能？

options.en: Naming a predicted benefit and an actual obstacle.
options.zh: 列出預期好處及實際障礙。

options.en: Repeating the same unqualified claim without showing a contrast.
options.zh: 重複相同且無保留的主張，沒有任何對照。

options.en: Distinguishing a proposal from the conditions in which it must operate.
options.zh: 區分提案與它實行時需面對的條件。

contrast.explanationZh: 兩部分需有有意義對照，不只是用but連接重複句。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想因網上表格理論較簡單就取消電話，但幾位常客連線仍不穩。哪句最好？

options.en: It is simpler in theory, but we should retain the phone route until those visitors have a workable alternative.
options.zh: 它理論上較簡單，但那些訪客未有可行替代前，仍應保留電話渠道。

options.en: We can remove the phone route now and find out about access problems after booking closes.
options.zh: 我們可現在取消電話，預約截止後才了解使用問題。

options.en: We should reject the online form even for visitors who have asked to use it.
options.zh: 即使有訪客要求用網上表格，我們也應拒絕。

dialogue.explanationZh: 針對實際限制保留渠道，不把預期當驗證，也不擴成反對所有網上使用。

speaking.en: The plan works in theory, but we need to check whether the available room and time support it in practice.
speaking.zh: 計劃理論上可行，但我們需核對實際房間及時間是否足以支持。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把預期連到具體條件。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你剪訪談片，原想每段只留十秒讓節奏快，試看卻發現觀眾未聽清人物關係。你想向同伴說明需保留兩段較長背景，不把整個短片構思推翻。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: In theory, ten-second clips keep the film moving, but our viewers missed the relationships between the speakers. We should keep two longer passages for context.
examples.zh: 理論上，十秒片段令影片節奏快，但觀眾沒弄清說話者關係；我們應保留兩段較長內容交代背景。

examples.en: The short-clip rule seems efficient in theory, but the viewing test showed a loss of context. Longer introductions for two speakers could solve that problem without abandoning the whole format.
examples.zh: 短片段規則理論上似有效率，但試看顯示失去背景；為兩位說話者保留較長介紹，可處理問題而不放棄整個形式。

writing.selfCheckZh: 用試看結果說明背景流失，提出局部延長，不把快節奏一概說成無用。

takeaways.en: In theory, one shared cupboard saves space, but the two groups need access at the same time.
takeaways.zh: 理論上共用一個櫃節省空間，但兩組需同時使用。

takeaways.en: The route is shorter in theory, but the closed gate means we cannot use it today.
takeaways.zh: 路線理論上較短，但門關了，今天不能走。

lessons.titleZh: 填入空格中缺少的內容

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Students can fill in the blanks but still struggle to converse.

brief.meaningEn: Supply the missing items in spaces provided in a text or exercise.
brief.meaningZh: 在文章或練習預留的空格，填上缺少的內容。
brief.grammar: fill in the blanks; filled/filling; in this lesson the literal conventional exercise instruction, not inventing unknown facts.
brief.register: Conventional classroom phrase; source category retained, although its described action is not figurative.
brief.boundaryZh: 填對空格只證明該任務的表現，不自動代表能自由對話或所有理解已掌握。
brief.misconceptionZh: 空格需按資料或題意填，不應以猜想當已核實資料。
brief.outcomeZh: 能區分指定填補與自由表達，並知道何時需查資料。

listening.promptZh: 練習成績與對話表現怎樣不同？

options.en: They completed the form-based task correctly but still needed practice using it in conversation.
options.zh: 他們填詞形正確，但仍需練習在對話運用。

options.en: They left the past-tense spaces empty.
options.zh: 他們把過去式空格留白。

options.en: They already spoke about yesterday without any pauses.
options.zh: 他們已能不停頓地說昨天的事。

options.en: The exercise asked only for future plans.
options.zh: 練習只要求將來計劃。

listening.explanationZh: 填對詞形與自由描述有不同要求；對話停頓仍需另練。
listening.en: The learners could fill in the blanks with the correct past-tense forms, but in a conversation they still paused when they tried to describe what happened yesterday.
listening.zh: 學習者能在空格填對過去式，但對話時想說昨天發生的事，仍會停頓。

reply.promptEn: Why are you adding conversation practice after the written exercise?
reply.promptZh: 書面練習後，你為甚麼加對話練習？

options.en: The learners can complete the written forms but still pause when describing yesterday.
options.zh: 學習者能完成書面詞形，但說昨天的事仍停頓。

options.en: They can fill in the blanks, but they still need to use those forms in conversation.
options.zh: 他們能填空，但仍需把那些詞形用在對話。

options.en: The written task does not yet show how easily they can tell a story aloud.
options.zh: 書面任務尚未顯示他們能否流暢地口述故事。

options.en: We want to connect the accurate written answers with spoken use.
options.zh: 我們想把準確書面答案連到口語運用。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都交代兩種任務的差距，不否定填空準確的價值。

scene.promptZh: 你替展覽整理物件表，表上留了年份空格；有些物件已有收據，另一些仍待查。哪句做法準確？

options.en: We can fill in the blanks from the receipts we have and mark the remaining dates as unconfirmed.
options.zh: 我們可按已有收據填空，把其餘日期標為未確認。

options.en: We can give every remaining object the date from the first receipt.
options.zh: 我們可把第一張收據的日期填到所有其餘物件。

options.en: The empty spaces show that all the dates have already been checked.
options.zh: 空格表示所有日期已核對。

scene.explanationZh: 用相應收據填已知部分，未知仍標示，不能把空格或單項日期當全部證據。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 learners can fill in the blanks 推出？

options.en: They supplied items required by that exercise.
options.zh: 他們填上該練習所需內容。

options.en: They can already use the language freely in any conversation.
options.zh: 他們已能在任何對話自由運用語言。

options.en: Another task may be needed to examine spontaneous use.
options.zh: 可能需另一任務檢視即時運用。

contrast.explanationZh: 指定空格的表現不等於所有即時對話能力。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想因學生填空全對，就刪去原定口述練習；先前對話仍有停頓。哪句最好？

options.en: They can fill in the blanks accurately, so let us build on that with a short conversation rather than treating the two tasks as identical.
options.zh: 他們能準確填空，所以一起以此為基礎練短對話，不把兩種任務視為相同吧。

options.en: We can use the written score as the result of a conversation we have not held.
options.zh: 我們可把書面分數當作尚未進行的對話成績。

options.en: We should repeat only the same written page and postpone speaking until the end of the year.
options.zh: 我們應只重做同一書面頁，把口說延至年末。

dialogue.explanationZh: 以已掌握填空為基礎增加口說資料，不假稱未做的任務已有結果。

speaking.en: Please fill in the blanks using the information provided, and leave a note where the date is still uncertain.
speaking.zh: 請按所提供的資料填空；日期仍不確定的地方，請留註記。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把填補與資料依據連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你設計故事工作紙，保留三個空格讓讀者選人物行動，後頁要求解釋其中一個選擇。你要寫清楚活動指示，區分填選擇與後續理由。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: Fill in the blanks with the actions you choose for the character. Then explain one choice on the next page using a detail from the story.
examples.zh: 在空格填上你為角色選的行動；然後在下一頁用故事的一項細節解釋其中一個選擇。

examples.en: You can fill in the blanks before writing your explanation. Choose one action afterwards and show how it fits the character’s situation.
examples.zh: 你可先填空，再寫解釋；之後選一項行動，說明它如何配合角色處境。

writing.selfCheckZh: 指示先填所選行動，再用故事細節解釋一項；不要把自由選擇當只有一個固定答案。

takeaways.en: We filled in the blanks using the recorded dates rather than guessing the missing ones.
takeaways.zh: 我們按已記錄日期填空，而非猜缺少的日期。

takeaways.en: After the class filled in the blanks, the pairs compared the reasons behind their choices.
takeaways.zh: 全班填空後，各組比較選擇背後的理由。

lessons.titleEn: make the leap into real life
lessons.titleZh: 跨到實際生活中運用

target.pattern: \bmak(?:e|es|ing) the leap into real life\b|\bmade the leap into real life\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Conversation practice helps grammar make the leap into real life.
sources.expression: make the leap into real life

brief.meaningEn: Move from an idea, exercise or theory into practical use outside that setting.
brief.meaningZh: 從構想、練習或理論，跨到該情境以外的實際運用。
brief.grammar: make the leap into real life; made/making; identify what is transferred and how the real task differs.
brief.register: Conventional leap metaphor with a context-specific destination; figurative rather than a literal jump. Source set-phrase category refined to figurative teaching frame.
brief.boundaryZh: 真正運用需有具體任務，不只把相同答案搬到另一頁；一次成功也不保證所有情境熟練。
brief.misconceptionZh: 實用與理論可互相支持，不表示學到基礎後便不需練習。
brief.outcomeZh: 能描述所學怎在真實需要中被調整運用。

options.en: The group adapted practised questions to an unexpected response in an actual interview.
options.zh: 小組在實際訪談，按意料外的回應調整練過的問題。

options.en: They copied the questions onto another practice sheet without interviewing anyone.
options.zh: 他們只把問題抄到另一張練習紙，沒有訪問任何人。

options.en: They kept the exact order and ignored the visitor’s response.
options.zh: 他們維持原次序，不理訪客回應。

options.en: They abandoned questions and read an unrelated prepared speech.
options.zh: 他們放棄提問，讀無關的預備演說。

listening.explanationZh: 實際對象的意外回應要求調整問題，顯示不只是重複練習紙。
listening.en: The interview questions made the leap into real life when our group used them at the neighbourhood archive, changing the order to follow the visitor’s unexpected story instead of reading the practice sheet straight through.
listening.zh: 小組在街坊檔案庫使用訪談問題，並按訪客出乎意料的故事調整次序，而非直讀練習紙時，問題便跨到實際生活中運用。

reply.promptEn: How did the practice questions help at the archive?
reply.promptZh: 練習問題怎樣幫助檔案庫的訪談？

options.en: They gave us a starting point that we adapted to the visitor’s story.
options.zh: 它們提供起點，我們再按訪客故事調整。

options.en: They made the leap into real life when we used and reordered them during the interview.
options.zh: 我們在訪談使用並重排它們時，它們便跨到實際生活中運用。

options.en: We drew on the preparation while responding to something we had not rehearsed.
options.zh: 我們回應未排練過的內容時，運用了事前準備。

options.en: The questions supported a real exchange rather than just another written exercise.
options.zh: 問題支持實際交流，而不只是另一份書面練習。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都連到實際交流與調整，不聲稱準備已列出所有可能答案。

scene.promptZh: 你學過按比例畫圖，現在替鄰居做書架草圖，實際量到門框較窄，便修正搬運尺寸。哪句準確？

options.en: The drawing skills made the leap into real life when I adapted the plan to the actual doorway.
options.zh: 我按實際門框調整方案時，繪圖技能便跨到生活中運用。

options.en: I only copied the sample drawing and did not check the doorway.
options.zh: 我只抄示範圖，沒有核對門框。

options.en: The doorway measurements were unnecessary because the sample had dimensions.
options.zh: 示範圖有尺寸，所以不需量門框。

scene.explanationZh: 所學用於實際尺寸限制，與重抄示範不同。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 make the leap into real life？

options.en: Using a learned method to address a new practical need.
options.zh: 用所學方法處理新的實際需要。

options.en: Copying an answer to another page without using it for a practical task.
options.zh: 把答案抄到另一頁，沒有用於實際任務。

options.en: Adapting a rehearsed skill when actual conditions differ.
options.zh: 實際條件不同時，調整排練過的技能。

contrast.explanationZh: 單純轉抄位置不構成實際運用；需有任務及條件。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把檔案庫訪談寫成完全照讀成功，但你們其實按訪客故事重排問題。哪句最好？

options.en: The questions made the leap into real life because we adapted them to the exchange, not because we followed the sheet unchanged.
options.zh: 問題因我們按交流調整而跨到實際運用，不是因原封不動照讀。

options.en: The visitor exchange shows that the prepared sequence needed no adaptation.
options.zh: 與訪客交流顯示，預備次序不需任何調整。

options.en: The unexpected story showed that our prepared questions could not contribute anything.
options.zh: 意料外的故事顯示，我們預備問題完全不能有幫助。

dialogue.explanationZh: 實際交流讓我們調整預備問題，並非原次序不需變；意外回應也不表示準備全無幫助。

speaking.en: The method made the leap into real life when we adjusted it to solve a problem outside the classroom.
speaking.zh: 我們調整方法去處理課室外的問題時，它便跨到實際生活中運用。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再說清轉用情境及所作調整。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在戲劇課學過留停頓讓對方接話，現在帶首次到訪者參觀時，發現急着講令對方插不上問題；你改在每區留提問時間。用一至兩句英文寫反思。

examples.en: The pause technique made the leap into real life when I used it to let visitors ask questions during the tour. I stopped filling every gap with more explanation.
examples.zh: 我在導賞時用停頓讓訪客提問，停頓技巧便跨到生活中運用；我不再把每個空隙都填上更多解說。

examples.en: A skill from drama class could make the leap into real life by changing how I guide visitors. Leaving time for questions makes the tour a conversation rather than a continuous speech.
examples.zh: 戲劇課技能可透過改變導賞方式跨到實際運用；留時間提問，令導賞成為對話，而非連續演說。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把停頓由舞台互動轉用到導賞提問，說明具體改變，不只寫學過戲劇便能帶團。

takeaways.en: The budgeting exercise made the leap into real life when the group compared actual printing quotes.
takeaways.zh: 小組比較實際印刷報價時，預算練習便跨到生活中運用。

takeaways.en: Her sketching method made the leap into real life when she used it to explain the room layout to the volunteers.
takeaways.zh: 她用速寫方法向義工解釋房間佈局時，所學便跨到實際生活中運用。

english.evidence: Productive transfer metaphor. Interview adaptation, measured drawing and conversational use of theatrical pauses involve different tools and practical mechanisms; not one exercise renamed.

chinese.evidence: Traditional Chinese checked against English subjects, negation, tense and modality; no independent human approval claimed.

lessons.titleZh: 只埋首課本而沒有實際運用

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A language cannot be mastered by living inside textbooks.

brief.meaningEn: Rely only on textbook study rather than engaging in direct use or experience.
brief.meaningZh: 只依靠課本學習，而未參與直接運用或體驗。
brief.grammar: live/living inside textbooks; explain the contrast between studying an account and acting outside that setting.
brief.register: Creative enclosure metaphor. It criticises exclusive reliance, not the existence or value of textbooks.
brief.boundaryZh: 讀課本與直接體驗可互補，不需拒絕參考資料；也不由比喻判所有書本內容不真實。
brief.misconceptionZh: 反對只看不做，不等於未有基礎便隨意行動。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出把讀到的內容連到具體實際觀察或交流的任務。

options.en: Questions grounded in a resident’s actual access experience.
options.zh: 以居民實際通行經驗為依據的問題。

options.en: Proof that none of the chapter’s information was accurate.
options.zh: 證明章節中沒有任何資料準確。

options.en: Another copy of the chapter with the same questions.
options.zh: 問題完全相同的另一份章節複本。

options.en: A decision to avoid talking to residents about the route.
options.zh: 避免與居民談路線的決定。

listening.explanationZh: 直接經驗增加課本未涵蓋的問題，不代表整章資料錯。
listening.en: We were living inside textbooks when we discussed neighbourhood change only through the sample chapter; walking the route with a resident revealed questions about access that the chapter did not cover.
listening.zh: 我們只按示範章節討論街區改變，像活在課本裏；跟居民走一次路線後，發現章節沒涵蓋的通行問題。

reply.promptEn: Why did you add the walk with a resident?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼加上與居民走路線的活動？

options.en: The chapter did not show all the access issues people encountered.
options.zh: 章節未展示人們遇到的所有通行問題。

options.en: We had been living inside textbooks and needed to connect the account with direct experience.
options.zh: 我們一直只活在課本裏，需要把記述連到直接經驗。

options.en: The resident could help us notice practical questions beyond the sample.
options.zh: 居民可幫我們留意示例以外的實際問題。

options.en: We wanted observations from the route to inform our discussion of change.
options.zh: 我們想以路線觀察幫助討論改變。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都給出直接觀察的作用，不把課本與居民經驗對立成只可選一。

scene.promptZh: 你讀了植物辨認手冊，現想在帶領下比較公園實物，記下哪些特徵難判。哪句貼切？

options.en: I do not want to keep living inside textbooks; comparing actual plants will show where I need more practice.
options.zh: 我不想一直只活在課本裏；比較真植物可顯示哪裏需多練。

options.en: The manual alone gives me enough evidence to label uncertain plants without comparing their features on site.
options.zh: 只靠手冊已有足夠依據標示不確定植物，不需實地比較特徵。

options.en: The walk requires us to stop using reference material for uncertain features.
options.zh: 這次步行要求我們遇不確定特徵也停止查參考資料。

scene.explanationZh: 實物比較可檢視哪些特徵難判；手冊可支援，卻不能代替實地比較，遇不確定仍可查參考。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 living inside textbooks 的批評推出？

options.en: Study limited to texts may miss direct experience.
options.zh: 只限文字的學習可能欠直接體驗。

options.en: Textbooks should never be consulted again.
options.zh: 從此不應再查課本。

options.en: Reading can be connected with observation or use.
options.zh: 閱讀可與觀察或運用連起來。

contrast.explanationZh: 批評只依賴課本，不是全面禁用課本。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說走路線後應把章節全刪，但部分背景仍有幫助。哪句最好？

options.en: We need not keep living inside textbooks, but we can use the chapter as background while checking it against observations.
options.zh: 我們不需一直只活在課本裏，但可用章節作背景，並與觀察核對。

options.en: The walk makes the useful background irrelevant, so we should omit it.
options.zh: 步行令有用背景也變無關，所以應省略。

options.en: We should ignore the resident’s access questions because they are absent from the sample.
options.zh: 居民的通行問題不在示例，所以應忽略。

dialogue.explanationZh: 把文字背景及實地問題互相對照，不因來源不同而全部排斥。

speaking.en: I had been living inside textbooks until the field visit gave me a reason to question the neat examples.
speaking.zh: 實地參觀讓我有理由追問那些整齊示例前，我一直只活在課本裏。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再連到實際經驗增加的問題。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你學過訪談倫理，現在要第一次邀請鄰居分享回憶。你想把書上原則化成清楚的邀請，讓對方知道可拒答或稍後撤回，不只背定義。用一至兩句英文寫準備反思。

examples.en: I do not want to keep living inside textbooks, so I will turn the consent principles into a clear invitation. My neighbour should know that questions can be declined and permission withdrawn later.
examples.zh: 我不想仍只活在課本裏，所以會把同意原則化成清楚邀請；鄰居應知道可以拒答，稍後也可撤回許可。

examples.en: Instead of living inside textbooks and reciting definitions, I will practise explaining the choices my neighbour has before agreeing to the interview.
examples.zh: 與其只活在課本裏背定義，我會練習在鄰居答應訪談前，解釋對方有哪些選擇。

writing.selfCheckZh: 把原則轉成對方能明白的邀請及選擇，不把參與當義務，也不只重述定義。

takeaways.en: The ecology class stopped living inside textbooks long enough to compare the stream observations with the diagram.
takeaways.zh: 生態課暫時走出只活在課本裏的狀態，把溪流觀察與圖表比較。

takeaways.en: Living inside textbooks had left me unprepared for the different questions the visitors actually asked.
takeaways.zh: 只活在課本裏，令我未能準備好應付訪客實際提出的不同問題。
