lessons.titleEn: less like a wall and more like a bridge
lessons.titleZh: 少一點障礙，多一點連接

target.pattern: \bless like a wall and more like a bridge\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Good feedback makes the task less like a wall and more like a bridge.
sources.expression: less like a wall and more like a bridge

brief.meaningEn: Describe something as becoming less of a barrier and more of a way to connect or make progress.
brief.meaningZh: 形容事物較少成為阻礙，較多成為連接或前進的方法。
brief.grammar: make/become/feel less like a wall and more like a bridge; explain both the obstacle and the connection.
brief.register: Paired creative structural metaphors, not a claim that all difficulty disappears.
brief.boundaryZh: 需具體障礙及連接做法，不把較易參與說成不需努力或已完成任務。
brief.misconceptionZh: 協助前進不等於替人完成，也不代表免去必要要求。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用對比說明某安排怎幫助跨過障礙。

options.en: It provides a usable way to approach the revision.
options.zh: 它提供可運用的修訂方向。

options.en: The tutor has already written the final ending for the group.
options.zh: 導師已替小組寫好最終結尾。

options.en: The ending no longer needs any attention.
options.zh: 結尾不再需處理。

options.en: The comments repeat only that the ending is weak without a next step.
options.zh: 評語只重複結尾弱，沒有下一步。

listening.explanationZh: 問題把批評連到可行下一步，不是代寫或取消修訂。
listening.en: The tutor’s comments made revision feel less like a wall and more like a bridge: instead of only marking the weak ending, she showed one question that could help us connect it to the opening.
listening.zh: 導師評語令修訂較不像一道牆，較像一座橋；她不只指出結尾弱，還示範一條問題，幫我們把結尾連到開頭。

reply.promptEn: Why did the tutor’s comments help you start revising?
reply.promptZh: 導師評語為甚麼幫你開始修訂？

options.en: She gave us a question that linked the ending to the opening.
options.zh: 她給一條問題，把結尾與開頭連起來。

options.en: The comments made revision less like a wall and more like a bridge by showing a next step.
options.zh: 評語展示下一步，令修訂較不像牆，較像橋。

options.en: We could see how to work on the problem rather than only hearing that it was weak.
options.zh: 我們看見怎處理問題，而不只聽到它弱。

options.en: Her feedback connected the criticism with something we could try ourselves.
options.zh: 她的回饋把批評連到我們可自己嘗試的做法。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都指出由障礙感轉到可採取行動的原因，仍由學生修訂。

scene.promptZh: 報名頁原本只列專門術語，改成按用途解釋並保留術語對照，新人較能選合適活動。哪句貼切？

options.en: The explanations make the page less like a wall and more like a bridge for new participants.
options.zh: 解釋令網頁對新人較不像牆，較像橋。

options.en: The page gives plain descriptions but no matching technical labels.
options.zh: 網頁有淺白描述，卻沒有相應專門術語。

options.en: The changes removed the explanations and left only the technical terms.
options.zh: 改動刪去解釋，只留下專門術語。

scene.explanationZh: 用途解釋與術語對照並存，幫新人理解及選擇；不是刪去術語，也不是只留術語而刪解釋。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 less like a wall and more like a bridge 推出？

options.en: Something offers a more helpful route forward.
options.zh: 某事物提供較有幫助的前進途徑。

options.en: The remaining task has already been completed for the person.
options.zh: 餘下任務已由別人替那人完成。

options.en: Context should show what becomes easier to connect or approach.
options.zh: 情境應說明甚麼較易連接或着手。

contrast.explanationZh: 有途徑不等於工作已被代做。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把導師評語報成「老師替我們寫好結尾」，但她只給連結問題。哪句最好？

options.en: Her question made revision less like a wall and more like a bridge, but we still have to write and test the ending.
options.zh: 她的問題令修訂較不像牆、較像橋，但我們仍需寫結尾及試效果。

options.en: We can submit the comments themselves as our revised ending.
options.zh: 我們可把評語本身當修訂後結尾交上。

options.en: We should ignore the question because it does not contain a finished paragraph.
options.zh: 問題沒有完成段落，所以我們應忽略它。

dialogue.explanationZh: 可用提示仍需轉成自己作品，不把提示與代做混淆。

speaking.en: The explanation made the process less like a wall and more like a bridge, although I still needed to do the work.
speaking.zh: 解釋令過程較不像牆、較像橋，但我仍需自己完成工作。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再保留協助與自己行動的分別。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為新舊街坊安排故事交流，擔心一開始要長篇自介會令人卻步。你想用每人自選一張地方照片、可先聽後說的方式開始，幫大家找到共同話題。用一至兩句英文提出安排。

examples.en: A choice of local photographs could make the first meeting less like a wall and more like a bridge. People could begin with a shared place and choose when to tell their story.
examples.zh: 提供地方照片選擇，可令首次聚會較不像牆、較像橋；大家可從共同地方開始，自選何時講故事。

examples.en: Letting people listen before speaking could make introductions less like a wall and more like a bridge between neighbours. A photograph can offer a topic without requiring a long personal account.
examples.zh: 讓大家先聽後說，可令自介較不像牆、較像街坊間的橋；照片可提供話題，而不要求長篇個人敘述。

writing.selfCheckZh: 交代降低初次交流門檻的方法及選擇空間，不保證所有人立即發言或成為好友。

takeaways.en: The bilingual notes made the exhibition less like a wall and more like a bridge for the visiting families.
takeaways.zh: 雙語說明令展覽對到訪家庭較不像牆、較像橋。

takeaways.en: A concrete example made the new method less like a wall and more like a bridge for our group.
takeaways.zh: 具體例子令新方法對我們小組較不像牆、較像橋。

lessons.titleZh: 小心迴避而未正面處理話題

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Learners need chances to speak instead of tiptoeing around it.

brief.meaningEn: Deal with a subject so cautiously or indirectly that it is not fully addressed.
brief.meaningZh: 過分小心或間接地處理話題，以致未有正面討論。
brief.grammar: tiptoe around + issue/question/it; tiptoed/tiptoeing; it needs a clear antecedent.
brief.register: Established movement metaphor for cautious avoidance. Being tactful is not necessarily avoiding the issue.
brief.boundaryZh: 需看實質問題是否被回應；尊重界線與含糊迴避不同，不要求揭露私人資料。
brief.misconceptionZh: 正面處理可以溫和，不等於質問或指責。
brief.outcomeZh: 能指出未處理的問題，提出具體而有禮的討論。

options.en: The practical question of who would check the room at closing.
options.zh: 誰在關門時檢查房間的實際問題。

options.en: Whether anyone had made an effort at all.
options.zh: 是否有人曾付出努力。

options.en: A room check that had already been assigned clearly to each evening.
options.zh: 每晚早已明確分派的房間檢查。

options.en: Whether the closing check had been completed before the meeting.
options.zh: 會議前是否已完成關門檢查。

listening.explanationZh: 稱讚沒有解決負責安排；明確姓名才回應未處理問題。
listening.en: We kept tiptoeing around the issue of missed handovers, praising everyone’s effort without agreeing who would check the room at closing time. Eventually we asked for one clear name on each evening’s list.
listening.zh: 我們一直小心迴避交接遺漏，只讚大家努力，未議定誰在關門時檢查房間；最後要求每晚清單列一位明確負責人。

reply.promptEn: Why did you ask for a name on each evening’s list?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼要求每晚清單列負責人姓名？

options.en: We had not settled who would do the closing check.
options.zh: 我們未定誰做關門檢查。

options.en: We were tiptoeing around the issue instead of agreeing a clear responsibility.
options.zh: 我們一直迴避問題，沒有議定明確責任。

options.en: Praise for the effort was not enough to prevent another missed handover.
options.zh: 讚賞努力不足以防止再漏交接。

options.en: The practical arrangement still needed a direct answer.
options.zh: 實際安排仍需直接回應。

reply.explanationZh: 四句回到未定責任，不把讚賞本身說成無價值。

scene.promptZh: 你訪問攝影者，對方不願講家庭私事，你尊重；但作品年份可公開確認，你仍只說照片漂亮，未問年份。哪句準確？

options.en: I am tiptoeing around the question of the date, even though she has agreed to discuss it.
options.zh: 她已同意談年份，我卻仍小心迴避這個問題。

options.en: Respecting her private boundary requires me to leave the public date unconfirmed too.
options.zh: 尊重她的私事界線，要求我連可公開年份也不確認。

options.en: She has already confirmed the date in the conversation.
options.zh: 她已在對話中確認年份。

scene.explanationZh: 分清受尊重的私人界線及已同意討論的年份，不把所有提問都混在一起。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不足以支持 tiptoeing around an issue？

options.en: Repeatedly praising effort while leaving the agreed practical question unanswered.
options.zh: 反覆讚努力，卻不回應已同意討論的實際問題。

options.en: Asking a specific question politely and accepting the person’s stated limits.
options.zh: 有禮地問具體問題，並接受對方表明的界線。

options.en: Speaking indirectly to avoid naming the arrangement that needs a decision.
options.zh: 間接說話，避免指出需作決定的安排。

contrast.explanationZh: 溫和而正面處理，不等於迴避。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說不再迴避就該責罵所有義工，但你只需確定誰關門檢查。哪句最好？

options.en: We can stop tiptoeing around the issue by agreeing a named checker, without blaming the whole group.
options.zh: 我們可議定具名檢查者，停止迴避問題，不需責怪整組人。

options.en: We should keep praising effort and leave the checker unnamed for another week.
options.zh: 我們應繼續讚努力，再一周不列檢查者姓名。

options.en: We should turn the check-in into a public complaint about each volunteer’s character.
options.zh: 我們應把跟進會變成公開批評每位義工品格。

dialogue.explanationZh: 正面處理實際責任，既不延後，也不改成品格指責。

speaking.en: We had not agreed who would check the room, and I kept tiptoeing around it instead of asking directly.
speaking.zh: 我們未議定誰檢查房間，而我一直小心迴避它，沒有直接問。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把未定的檢查安排與迴避反應連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你和朋友合寫劇本，兩人都覺得某場太長，卻一直只改標點。你想發訊息溫和提出試刪一段重複對白，再比較節奏，不批評朋友能力。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We have been tiptoeing around the issue by changing punctuation while the scene stays too long. Could we try cutting the repeated exchange and compare the pace?
examples.zh: 我們一直改標點、讓場面仍太長，實在迴避問題；可否試刪重複對白，比較節奏？

examples.en: Rather than tiptoe around the question of length, let us test a shorter version of the scene. We can compare the rhythm without making it a judgement about either writer.
examples.zh: 與其迴避長度問題，不如試較短版本；我們可比較節奏，不把它變成對任何一位作者的評斷。

writing.selfCheckZh: 明確提出過長及可逆的刪段比較，保持合作語氣，不停留表面修改，也不攻擊能力。

takeaways.en: The committee had tiptoed around the cost question until someone asked which items were actually funded.
takeaways.zh: 有人問哪些項目實際有資助前，委員會一直迴避費用問題。

takeaways.en: I stopped tiptoeing around it and asked whether the two deadlines could both be met.
takeaways.zh: 我不再小心迴避它，直接問兩個限期能否兼顧。

lessons.titleZh: 找到自信表達自己的方式

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: The drama club helped shy students find their voice.

brief.meaningEn: Develop the confidence or a distinctive way to express ideas or feelings.
brief.meaningZh: 逐漸有信心，或找到有自己特色的方式，表達想法或感受。
brief.grammar: find one’s voice; found/finding; distinguish confidence or style from literal recovery of speech.
brief.register: Established expression for personal expression, also used of a writer’s developing style. It does not require becoming loud or imitating the group.
brief.boundaryZh: 表達自信可在小組或文字中出現，不表示性格全面外向、人人認同或風格已固定。
brief.misconceptionZh: 可受支援而找到自己的表達，不等於別人替他說。
brief.outcomeZh: 能用具體改變說明表達如何發展。

options.en: He explained his own view rather than merely repeating the dominant opinion.
options.zh: 他解釋自己的看法，不再只重複強勢意見。

options.en: He adopted the strongest opinion without giving a reason of his own.
options.zh: 他接受最強勢意見，沒有給自己的理由。

options.en: Everyone changed their preference to match his ending.
options.zh: 人人改變喜好，配合他的結尾。

options.en: Another reviewer wrote and delivered his explanation for him.
options.zh: 另一位評閱者替他寫並講出解釋。

listening.explanationZh: 自己的理由及保留不同意見顯示表達自信，不需所有人認同。
listening.en: In the small review circle, Jae began to find his voice: he stopped copying the strongest opinion and explained why the quieter ending mattered to him, even when others preferred a different version.
listening.zh: 在小型評閱圈中，傑開始找到自己的表達方式；他不再照搬最強勢意見，而解釋安靜結尾對他為何重要，即使其他人偏愛另一版。

reply.promptEn: How did Jae’s participation change in the review circle?
reply.promptZh: 傑在評閱圈的參與怎樣改變？

options.en: He began explaining what mattered to him in the ending.
options.zh: 他開始解釋結尾中甚麼對他重要。

options.en: He began to find his voice instead of echoing the strongest opinion.
options.zh: 他開始找到自己的表達，而非附和最強勢意見。

options.en: His own reasons became part of the discussion even when others disagreed.
options.zh: 即使別人不同意，他自己的理由也進入討論。

options.en: He could state a preference without needing the group to share it.
options.zh: 他可表明喜好，不需整組人都同意。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說自己的表達進入交流，不把它等同獲全票支持。

scene.promptZh: 一位初寫詩的人試過模仿幾位作者，後來用自己習慣的短句及街坊聲音寫出個人風格。哪句貼切？

options.en: She is finding her voice through the rhythms and sounds she knows.
options.zh: 她透過熟悉的節奏及聲音，找到自己的寫作聲音。

options.en: She is copying one poet’s lines without making choices of her own.
options.zh: 她照抄一位詩人的句子，沒有自己取捨。

options.en: Finding a style means she has decided never to revise another poem.
options.zh: 找到風格表示她決定不再修改任何詩。

scene.explanationZh: 可用於寫作風格發展，不限音量或當眾說話。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 find their voice 推出？

options.en: People develop a way to express their own ideas.
options.zh: 人們發展出表達自己想法的方式。

options.en: Their audience must agree with what they express.
options.zh: 聽眾必須認同他們所表達的內容。

options.en: Their expression may become more confident or distinctive.
options.zh: 他們的表達可能更自信或有特色。

contrast.explanationZh: 表達能力或個人特色不等於觀眾必同意。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴說傑找到聲音後，就該放棄安靜結尾以配合多數；但他有自己的理由。哪句最好？

options.en: Finding his voice lets him explain the choice; the group can consider his reasons without requiring him to echo the majority.
options.zh: 找到自己的表達讓他能解釋選擇；小組可考慮理由，不需他附和多數。

options.en: He should hold his view back until the group has finished revising the scene.
options.zh: 他應等小組修好場景後，才提出自己的看法。

options.en: We should dismiss his explanation because the group has not agreed with it.
options.zh: 小組未同意，所以應排斥他的解釋。

dialogue.explanationZh: 自己的理由應能進入修訂討論，不需等修好才說，也不因未獲認同便被排斥。

speaking.en: She found her voice by explaining what she noticed, not by trying to sound like the loudest person in the room.
speaking.zh: 她透過解釋自己的觀察找到表達方式，不是模仿房中最大聲的人。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再區分個人表達與附和音量。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你是社區報義工，想邀一直只交照片的街坊試加一句自己的觀察，可先用筆名，並由本人確認編輯改動。你要寫一段邀請，給對方嘗試表達的空間，不替對方寫立場。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: A short observation beside your photograph could give you room to find your voice in the newsletter. You can begin under a pen name and approve any edits before publication.
examples.zh: 在照片旁加一句短觀察，可給你在通訊中嘗試自己表達的空間；你可先用筆名，並在刊登前確認任何編輯改動。

examples.en: We would like to help you find your voice by inviting one detail you noticed, rather than writing an opinion for you. A pen name is welcome, and you can review the edited line.
examples.zh: 我們想邀你寫一項親眼留意的細節，幫你找到自己的表達，而不替你寫意見；歡迎用筆名，你也可審閱修訂句子。

writing.selfCheckZh: 以簡短親身觀察、筆名及本人審閱提供自選表達空間，不代寫立場或把邀請當答應刊登。

takeaways.en: The newcomer found her voice when the group gave her time to explain a different approach.
takeaways.zh: 小組給新人時間解釋另一方法時，她找到自信表達。

takeaways.en: Our newsletter found its voice in the small observations contributed by residents.
takeaways.zh: 街坊投稿的小觀察，讓我們的通訊找到自己的風格。

lessons.titleZh: 設定更有挑戰的目標

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A good mentor helps us aim higher.

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A good mentor helps us aim higher.

brief.meaningEn: Set a more ambitious goal or standard than before.
brief.meaningZh: 設定比以前更有挑戰的目標或標準。
brief.grammar: aim higher; aimed/aiming; state the previous level and the proposed challenge.
brief.register: Common ambition metaphor; higher refers to aspiration, not necessarily rank, money or physical height.
brief.boundaryZh: 較高目標仍需配合資源及步驟，不代表原有工作差或新目標必達成。
brief.misconceptionZh: 目標提高與只增加工作量不同；要說明想改善甚麼。
brief.outcomeZh: 能提出具體挑戰及可行試行安排。

options.en: Extending the guide to serve visitors arriving from more starting points.
options.zh: 擴充指南，幫從更多出發點到來的訪客。

options.en: Reprinting the same entrance information without adding another route.
options.zh: 重印相同入口資料，沒有增加另一條路線。

options.en: Claiming all the new routes had already been tested.
options.zh: 聲稱所有新路線早已測試。

options.en: Removing the successful entrance information without adding a new purpose.
options.zh: 刪去有效的入口資料，沒有新增目的。

listening.explanationZh: 新挑戰是更多出發點，先試一條保留發展步驟，未報成全已驗證。
listening.en: After our first short guide helped visitors find the entrance, we decided to aim higher by adding routes for different starting points; we would test one new route before expanding the whole guide.
listening.zh: 首份短指南幫訪客找到入口後，我們決定提高目標，加入不同出發點的路線；全面擴充前會先測一條新路線。

reply.promptEn: Why are you planning routes from different starting points?
reply.promptZh: 你為甚麼規劃不同出發點的路線？

options.en: The first guide worked, and we want it to help a wider range of visitors.
options.zh: 首份指南有效，我們想幫更多不同訪客。

options.en: We want to aim higher by extending the guide beyond one entrance route.
options.zh: 我們想提高目標，把指南擴充到不只一條入口路線。

options.en: The next challenge is to make the guide useful from more locations.
options.zh: 下一個挑戰是令指南在更多地點起步也有用。

options.en: We are building on the first result with a more demanding purpose.
options.zh: 我們以首個成果為基礎，設定更有挑戰的目的。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都提出具體新用途，不把舊成果否定或新計劃當已完成。

scene.promptZh: 你會照譜彈奏，現在想為一首歌寫簡單伴奏，先試四小節，再請老師聽。哪句合適？

options.en: I want to aim higher by trying an accompaniment of my own in a small first step.
options.zh: 我想提高目標，先小規模嘗試自己的伴奏。

options.en: I plan to copy someone else’s accompaniment unchanged rather than try four bars of my own.
options.zh: 我打算原樣抄別人的伴奏，而非試自己四小節。

options.en: Playing the same notes louder is the only change I have planned.
options.zh: 我計劃的唯一改動是把同樣音符彈得更大聲。

scene.explanationZh: 由照譜到試自己四小節伴奏是新挑戰；不是照搬別人伴奏，也不只把原音符彈更大聲。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜只憑 aim higher 推出？

options.en: Someone is setting a more ambitious goal.
options.zh: 有人設定更有挑戰的目標。

options.en: The new goal has already been achieved.
options.zh: 新目標已經達成。

options.en: The context may explain the next level of challenge.
options.zh: 情境可能解釋下一層挑戰。

contrast.explanationZh: 追求較高目標與已實現不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說提高指南目標就應同日加完所有路線，但你們只安排先試一條。哪句最好？

options.en: We can aim higher while testing one route first; ambition does not remove the need to check the details.
options.zh: 我們可提高目標，同時先試一條路線；志向不會取代核對細節。

options.en: We should publish all the routes now and use the first test as proof for the untested ones.
options.zh: 我們應現在發布所有路線，把首條測試當未試路線的證據。

options.en: We should abandon the new purpose because it cannot be completed in one day.
options.zh: 新目的不能一天完成，所以應放棄。

dialogue.explanationZh: 具挑戰目標可分步驗證，不在未測或非即成之間二選一。

speaking.en: I want to aim higher, so I am choosing a specific new challenge and a first step I can test.
speaking.zh: 我想提高目標，所以正選一項具體新挑戰及可測試的第一步。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把志向連到實際步驟。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你答應替圖書角辦活動，去年只有單向朗讀；今年想邀參加者一起編兩種結尾，先用一段短故事試流程。你要向伙伴提出計劃，不只承諾人數增加。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We can aim higher than a read-aloud session by inviting people to create two endings together. A short story will let us test the activity before planning a longer programme.
examples.zh: 我們可提高目標，不只朗讀，而邀大家一起編兩種結尾；短故事可讓我們先試活動，再規劃較長節目。

examples.en: I want to aim higher by making the session a shared creative task. Let us try the two-ending exercise with one short passage first.
examples.zh: 我想提高目標，把活動變成共同創作；先用一小段試兩種結尾練習吧。

writing.selfCheckZh: 新挑戰是由聽朗讀轉向共同創作，先用短段測流程，不只說多做或承諾必成功。

takeaways.en: The young reporter aimed higher by learning to compare several accounts rather than quoting one source.
takeaways.zh: 年輕記者透過學習比較多份敘述、不只引一個來源，設定更有挑戰的目標。

takeaways.en: Our next draft can aim higher by giving the quieter character a meaningful choice.
takeaways.zh: 下一稿可提高目標，給較安靜角色一項有意義的選擇。

lessons.titleZh: 較具備做某事的有利條件

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Well-supported students are better placed to succeed.

brief.meaningEn: In a more favourable position or having more suitable resources to do something.
brief.meaningZh: 處於較有利位置，或具備較適合資源去做某事。
brief.grammar: be better placed to + verb; comparison should be clear or recoverable from context. Not simply physical location.
brief.register: Natural comparative pattern for capacity or circumstances, not a guarantee of success.
brief.boundaryZh: 要指出有利條件及比較基礎，不表示對方完全做不到或結果必成。
brief.misconceptionZh: 較適合提出資訊，不等於有權替別人決定。
brief.outcomeZh: 能按相關條件安排任務，保留角色及結果限制。

options.en: Lina had examined the original records, while the others had seen only a summary.
options.zh: 莉娜看過原始記錄，其他人只看過摘要。

options.en: Lina was standing nearer the booking desk during the meeting.
options.zh: 開會時莉娜站得較近預約櫃台。

options.en: The others had examined more original records than Lina.
options.zh: 其他人比莉娜看過更多原始記錄。

options.en: Lina had authority to change the bookings without consulting anyone.
options.zh: 莉娜有權不問任何人便改預約。

listening.explanationZh: 資訊差異支持解釋條件較佳，未交代站位或更改權限。
listening.en: Because Lina had checked the original booking records, she was better placed to explain the date changes than the rest of us, who had only seen the shortened notice.
listening.zh: 莉娜核對過原始預約記錄，而我們其餘人只看過簡短通告，所以她較有條件解釋日期改動。

reply.promptEn: Why should Lina explain the date changes first?
reply.promptZh: 為甚麼應先請莉娜解釋日期改動？

options.en: She has checked the original booking records.
options.zh: 她核對過原始預約記錄。

options.en: She is better placed to explain them because she has seen the records behind the notice.
options.zh: 她看過通告背後的記錄，所以較有條件解釋。

options.en: Her information is more complete than the summary the rest of us saw.
options.zh: 她的資料比我們其餘人看的摘要完整。

options.en: She can draw on the original dates rather than only the shortened announcement.
options.zh: 她可參考原始日期，而不只看簡短公告。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都有原始資料理由，不把較佳資訊變成單方面決策權。

scene.promptZh: 兩位組員都可整理訪談，阿明親自到場並記了聽不清的段落，小華只拿到轉錄稿。你要先查錄音背景。哪句準確？

options.en: Ming is better placed to explain the unclear moments because he was there and kept notes.
options.zh: 阿明在場且有筆記，所以較有條件解釋不清楚的地方。

options.en: Wah has already checked the pauses against the original audio.
options.zh: 小華已把停頓與原錄音核對。

options.en: Ming can settle the unclear wording without checking the recording again.
options.zh: 阿明不用再查錄音，便能確定不清楚的字句。

scene.explanationZh: 到場及筆記讓阿明較有條件解釋背景，但他仍可能需查錄音；小華則只拿到轉錄稿。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 better placed to do something 推出？

options.en: A person has relatively helpful conditions for a task.
options.zh: 某人具備對任務較有幫助的條件。

options.en: The task is guaranteed to succeed.
options.zh: 該任務保證成功。

options.en: The reason for the comparison should be relevant to the task.
options.zh: 比較理由應與任務相關。

contrast.explanationZh: 相對有利條件仍非結果保證。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說莉娜懂記錄，就可不用問場地方直接改日期；她只被請來解釋。哪句最好？

options.en: She is better placed to explain the records, but changing the booking still needs the venue’s agreement.
options.zh: 她較有條件解釋記錄，但改預約仍需場地方同意。

options.en: Her fuller information is enough to treat the new booking as confirmed.
options.zh: 她資料較完整，已足以把新預約當確認。

options.en: We should exclude her explanation because she does not control the venue.
options.zh: 她不控制場地，所以我們應排除她的解釋。

dialogue.explanationZh: 資訊作用與授權分清，並不因無決策權便排除有用解釋。

speaking.en: With the original notes, she is better placed to answer the question, although the final decision belongs to the group.
speaking.zh: 有原始筆記，她較有條件回答問題，但最後決定屬小組。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再區分相關條件與決策權。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：兩份候選路線都未試行，你們先走過其中一條，記下坡度及休息點。你想報告現在較能提出具體問題，卻仍不能斷言哪條最好。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: After walking the first route, we are better placed to ask specific questions about slopes and rest points. We still need to examine the second route before comparing them.
examples.zh: 走過首條路後，我們較有條件問坡度及休息點的具體問題；比較前，仍需檢視第二條。

examples.en: The visit leaves us better placed to discuss practical needs, but it does not settle which route is best. We have observations from only one option.
examples.zh: 參觀令我們較有條件討論實際需要，但未決定哪條路最好；我們只有一個選項的觀察。

writing.selfCheckZh: 有實地觀察所以問題更具體，但樣本只一條，保留第二條未查及未能評最好。

takeaways.en: The trial leaves us better placed to estimate how much preparation the next workshop needs.
takeaways.zh: 試行令我們較有條件估計下一個工作坊需多少準備。

takeaways.en: Having heard both accounts, the editor was better placed to identify the remaining questions.
takeaways.zh: 聽過兩份敘述後，編輯較有條件找出餘下問題。

lessons.titleZh: 指引某人找到有用方向或選項

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: Mentors can point them towards internships.

brief.meaningEn: Direct someone’s attention to a potentially useful resource, opportunity or next step.
brief.meaningZh: 把某人的注意引向可能有用的資源、機會或下一步。
brief.grammar: point someone towards + resource/opportunity; pointed/pointing; towards/toward can vary by dialect, teaching uses British towards.
brief.register: Figurative guidance sense of the directional verb pattern; source phrasal-verb category retained. Guidance is not doing the whole task or guaranteeing access.
brief.boundaryZh: 需交代指向甚麼及有何關係，不把介紹變成已獲錄取、批准或由介紹者代做。
brief.misconceptionZh: 人仍需選擇、查資料及完成下一步。
brief.outcomeZh: 能自然提出相關方向並保留申請或使用條件。

options.en: She directed the group to a relevant source that still required checking.
options.zh: 她指引小組到相關來源，但仍需核對。

options.en: She compared two reports and gave the group her conclusion about their dates.
options.zh: 她比較兩份報道，並給小組關於日期的結論。

options.en: She advised the group to stop looking for reports on the cinema.
options.zh: 她建議小組停止找戲院報道。

options.en: She told the group the archive contained no newspapers.
options.zh: 她告訴小組檔案中沒有報紙。

listening.explanationZh: 指出來源是提供方向，不等於完成核對。
listening.en: The librarian pointed us towards the local newspaper archive for reports on the old cinema, but we still had to compare dates and check which articles referred to the same building.
listening.zh: 圖書館員指引我們去本地報紙檔案找舊戲院報道，但我們仍需比較日期，核對哪些文章說同一座建築。

reply.promptEn: How did the librarian help your cinema research?
reply.promptZh: 圖書館員怎幫你們研究戲院？

options.en: She suggested the local newspaper archive as a source to search.
options.zh: 她建議搜尋本地報紙檔案。

options.en: She pointed us towards an archive that might contain relevant reports.
options.zh: 她指引我們去可能有相關報道的檔案。

options.en: Her advice gave us a useful starting place for finding reports.
options.zh: 她的建議給我們找報道的有用起點。

options.en: She showed us where to look, while we remained responsible for checking the articles.
options.zh: 她指明可到哪裏找，我們仍負責核對文章。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都說相關搜尋方向，不誇成替小組完成研究。

scene.promptZh: 朋友想練舞台化妝，你知道社區中心有入門班，但未問是否有位。哪句可準確推薦？

options.en: I can point you towards the centre’s beginner class, but you will need to check whether places are available.
options.zh: 我可指引你了解中心的入門班，但你需查是否有位。

options.en: My suggestion confirms that a place has already been reserved for you.
options.zh: 我的建議確認已有位置為你預留。

options.en: You can attend the first class and check whether a place is available afterwards.
options.zh: 你可先出席第一課，之後才查有沒有位。

scene.explanationZh: 可提供課程方向，但出席前應查名額；介紹不等於已預留，也不宜到課後才確認。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 point someone towards an opportunity 推出？

options.en: A person is directed to an option worth examining.
options.zh: 某人獲指引去了解值得看的選項。

options.en: Acceptance into the opportunity has already been guaranteed.
options.zh: 獲接受參與該機會已得到保證。

options.en: Further checking or action may still be needed.
options.zh: 仍可能需核對或行動。

contrast.explanationZh: 介紹方向與正式獲接受不同。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴想把圖書館員指引寫成她已核實所有戲院文章，但你們仍需比較。哪句最好？

options.en: She pointed us towards a useful source; the date and building checks are still our next steps.
options.zh: 她指引我們找到有用來源；日期及建築核對仍是我們下一步。

options.en: We can cite all the articles as verified because a librarian suggested the archive.
options.zh: 圖書館員建議這檔案，所以可把所有文章引作已核實。

options.en: We should stop using the source because it does not arrive with a completed comparison.
options.zh: 來源沒有附完成比較，所以我們應停止使用。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留指引的價值及研究者仍需完成的核對。

speaking.en: I can point you towards a useful contact, but you will need to ask about the conditions yourself.
speaking.zh: 我可指引你找到有用聯絡人，但你需親自問條件。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把提供方向與下一步分清。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你為街坊通訊寫一段服務資訊；居民問怎修舊椅，你只知道附近維修聚會可先看物件，收費及是否可修需由義工確認。你想提供方向，不替對方承諾結果。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: We can point residents towards the local repair meeting for an initial look at the chair. The volunteers will need to confirm the possible work and any charges.
examples.zh: 我們可指引居民到本地維修聚會，先讓人看看椅子；可能做哪些工序及費用，需由義工確認。

examples.en: The notice can point people towards the repair volunteers without promising a free or successful repair. Residents should ask what can be done after the chair is examined.
examples.zh: 通告可指引大家找維修義工，不承諾免費或一定修好；居民應待椅子檢視後，問可做甚麼。

writing.selfCheckZh: 在公共資訊中給查詢渠道，讓義工確認可修範圍及收費，不把介紹當保證。

takeaways.en: The tutor pointed her towards a collection of short scenes she could compare before writing.
takeaways.zh: 導師指引她去看一組可在寫作前比較的短場景。

takeaways.en: A neighbour pointed us towards the records office when we asked about the old shop names.
takeaways.zh: 我們問舊店名時，鄰居指引我們去記錄辦事處。

lessons.titleZh: 替別人走完必須親身走的路

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: A school can guide you, but it cannot walk the path for you.

brief.meaningEn: Do the personal effort or experience that another person must undertake for themselves.
brief.meaningZh: 代做另一人必須親身投入的努力或經歷。
brief.grammar: Someone can guide you but cannot walk the path for you; for + person; explain the help available and the work that remains personal.
brief.register: Creative journey metaphor for responsibility and experience; often used in a negative clause. It does not mean that support should be withdrawn.
brief.boundaryZh: 支援可有實質作用，個人仍需參與；不把需要協助說成懶惰或失敗。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不能代走不等於不應示範、陪伴或移除不必要障礙。
brief.outcomeZh: 能同時承認支援與自己須投入的工作。

listening.promptZh: 哪些工作仍需學生自己做？

options.en: Practising and making responsive choices during the scene.
options.zh: 練習，並在場景中按回應作選擇。

options.en: Receiving a finished performance that the tutor completed in their place.
options.zh: 接收導師代他們完成的演出。

options.en: Avoiding rehearsal because methods had already been suggested.
options.zh: 方法已獲建議，所以避開排練。

options.en: Rejecting any tutor guidance before attempting the scene.
options.zh: 試場景前拒絕所有導師指引。

listening.explanationZh: 指引可幫忙，但學生仍需親身練習及回應，不是拒絕支援。
listening.en: The tutor could suggest rehearsal methods, but she could not walk the path for us: we still had to practise the scene, listen to one another and decide how our characters would respond.
listening.zh: 導師可建議排練方法，但不能替我們走完這條路；我們仍需練場景、聽彼此，並決定角色怎回應。

reply.promptEn: Why do you still need to rehearse after the tutor’s advice?
reply.promptZh: 導師給建議後，你為甚麼仍需排練？

options.en: We need to practise responding to one another ourselves.
options.zh: 我們需親自練習回應彼此。

options.en: She can guide us, but she cannot walk the path for us; we still have to make the scene work together.
options.zh: 她可指引我們，但不能替我們走這條路；我們仍需一起把場景演好。

options.en: Knowing a method is not the same as doing the performance together.
options.zh: 知道方法不同於一起實際演出。

options.en: The advice gives us tools, while the rehearsal choices remain ours.
options.zh: 建議提供工具，排練取捨仍需我們自己做。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都保留指引與親身投入的分別，不把支援說成無用。

scene.promptZh: 朋友可陪你比較學科資料，但你需按自己的興趣及時間決定選修。你想表達謝意及責任。哪句貼切？

options.en: You can help me compare the options, but you cannot walk the path for me; I need to make the choice.
options.zh: 你可幫我比較選項，但不能替我走這條路；我需自己作選擇。

options.en: Your help means I no longer need to consider my own interests.
options.zh: 你的幫助表示我不再需考慮自己的興趣。

options.en: Making my own decision requires me to refuse the information you offer.
options.zh: 自己決定要求我拒絕你提供的資料。

scene.explanationZh: 資訊支援與個人選擇可並存，不把自主等同孤立。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 cannot walk the path for you 推出？

options.en: Some personal effort or choice cannot simply be delegated.
options.zh: 某些親身努力或選擇不能直接交人代做。

options.en: Useful guidance should be removed altogether.
options.zh: 所有有用指引都應撤走。

options.en: A helper may support the person without replacing their participation.
options.zh: 幫手可支援，而不取代當事人參與。

contrast.explanationZh: 不可代走不是不可幫。

dialogue.promptZh: 同伴以為老師不能代排練，就不應示範方法；示範原可幫大家開始。哪句最好？

options.en: She cannot walk the path for us, but a demonstration can help us begin practising it ourselves.
options.zh: 她不能替我們走這條路，但示範可幫我們開始親自練習。

options.en: We should cancel the demonstration and work without understanding the method.
options.zh: 我們應取消示範，在不明白方法下做。

options.en: We can submit the tutor’s demonstration as our own rehearsed scene.
options.zh: 我們可把導師示範當我們自己的排練場景交上。

dialogue.explanationZh: 保留有用示範，不以他人演示冒充親身實作。

speaking.en: My mentor can guide me, but she cannot walk the path for me; I still need to test the choices in my own work.
speaking.zh: 導師可指引我，但不能替我走這條路；我仍需在自己的作品中試驗取捨。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再把幫助與親身投入連起來。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你首次整理長者口述記錄，有同伴替你示範核對一段，但你仍需自己聽其餘錄音、標出不清字句，再請原講者確認。你想寫工作承諾，既感謝示範也不推卸責任。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: Your example helps, but you cannot walk the path for me: I must check the remaining recordings myself. I will listen carefully, mark unclear words and ask the speaker to confirm them.
examples.zh: 你的示範有幫助，但不能替我走這條路：餘下錄音須我親自核對；我會細聽、標不清字句，並請講者確認。

examples.en: I am grateful for the demonstration, although you cannot walk the path for me. I will use the method to check the recordings and keep uncertain words marked until the speaker responds.
examples.zh: 我感謝示範，但你不能替我走這條路；我會用該方法核對錄音，講者回覆前保留不確定字句的標記。

glossary.en: ask the speaker to confirm them

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認示範幫助，承諾親自細聽及回問確認，不把示範一段當其餘已查。

takeaways.en: Her adviser can explain the options but cannot walk the path for her; she must make the choice herself.
takeaways.zh: 顧問可解釋選項，但不能替她走這條路；她須自己作選擇。

takeaways.en: I could encourage him, but I could not walk the path for him; he had to practise the new skill himself.
takeaways.zh: 我可鼓勵他，但不能替他走這條路；他須親自練新技能。

lessons.titleZh: 決定你往後整段人生

target.pattern: \bwrit(?:e|es|ing) (?:my|your|his|her|our|their) whole future\b|\bwrote (?:my|your|his|her|our|their) whole future\b|\bwritten (?:my|your|his|her|our|their) whole future\b

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 2 to 9 Part 3.docx.pdf
sources.sentence: One exam cannot write your whole future.

brief.meaningEn: Portray a single event or influence as determining the whole of someone’s later life.
brief.meaningZh: 把單一事件或影響比作能決定某人往後整段人生。
brief.grammar: write someone’s whole future; often cannot/does not write...; wrote/written; writing a future is a creative authorship metaphor.
brief.register: Extended writing metaphor, often used to challenge an overly final judgement. Does not deny immediate consequences.
brief.boundaryZh: 不能決定一生，不等於事件沒有後果；需承認眼前影響及仍可採取的行動。
brief.misconceptionZh: 希望不是保證成功，也不是把已發生的損失說成不存在。
brief.outcomeZh: 能平衡單次結果的限制、實際影響及下一步選擇。

options.en: It matters now without determining every later opportunity.
options.zh: 它現在有影響，卻未決定日後每個機會。

options.en: It had no disappointing consequence at the time.
options.zh: 它當時沒有令人失望的後果。

options.en: It guaranteed her acceptance at the next workshop.
options.zh: 它保證她獲下次工作坊接受。

options.en: It had already fixed her choice to stop performing permanently.
options.zh: 它已確定她永久停止演出的選擇。

listening.explanationZh: 承認失望，也列出後續選擇；既非沒影響，也非保證下次結果。
listening.en: The unsuccessful audition was a real disappointment, but it did not write her whole future; after asking about the feedback, she chose to prepare a different piece for the next open workshop.
listening.zh: 試演未獲選令人真正失望，但它沒有寫定她整個未來；問過回饋後，她選擇為下次公開工作坊準備另一作品。

reply.promptEn: Why did she prepare another piece after the disappointment?
reply.promptZh: 失望之後，她為甚麼仍準備另一作品？

options.en: She still had choices about how to continue working.
options.zh: 她對怎樣繼續創作仍有選擇。

options.en: One unsuccessful audition did not write her whole future.
options.zh: 一次試演未獲選，沒有寫定她整個未來。

options.en: The setback did not settle every opportunity that might follow.
options.zh: 挫折未決定之後可能出現的每個機會。

options.en: She could recognise the loss while choosing another practical step.
options.zh: 她可承認失落，同時選另一實際步驟。

reply.explanationZh: 四句保留未來選擇，不假稱失落消失或下次一定成功。

scene.promptZh: 老師說你的首稿人物動機不清，建議用一段對白補線索；你想承認問題，而不說自己往後都不能寫。哪句貼切？

options.en: This feedback does not write my whole future; I can revise the dialogue to clarify the character’s motive.
options.zh: 這回饋未寫定我整個未來；我可修對白，說清角色動機。

options.en: The feedback says the first draft is already clear enough to publish unchanged.
options.zh: 回饋說首稿已夠清楚，可原樣刊登。

options.en: The first draft needs work, so I will stop trying revised versions.
options.zh: 首稿需修改，所以我會停止嘗試修訂版本。

scene.explanationZh: 回饋指出動機不清，並給修訂方向；可採取下一步，不把首稿當已可原樣刊登，也不以一次回饋定一生。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項最不宜由 does not write your whole future 推出？

options.en: One event need not determine every later outcome.
options.zh: 一事未必決定往後所有結果。

options.en: The event has no immediate consequences at all.
options.zh: 事件完全沒有即時後果。

options.en: Further choices may remain available.
options.zh: 仍可能有其他選擇。

contrast.explanationZh: 非決定一切，不等於完全無後果。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友想把安慰說成「下次必錄取」，你只知仍有其他練習途徑。哪句最好？

options.en: This does not write your whole future, but I cannot promise the next result; let us look at available ways to keep practising.
options.zh: 這未寫定你整個未來，但我不能保證下次結果；一起看看可繼續練習的方法吧。

options.en: The next place is yours already, even though nobody has confirmed it.
options.zh: 雖然無人確認，下個位置已屬於你。

options.en: You should stop seeking practice because the first result settles your ability.
options.zh: 首個結果已決定你能力，所以應停止找練習。

dialogue.explanationZh: 以未來選擇及具體查詢作支持，不給無根據錄取保證。

speaking.en: The result matters, but it does not write my whole future; I can still decide what to try next.
speaking.zh: 結果重要，但未寫定我整個未來；我仍可決定下一步試甚麼。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽，再兼顧影響與餘下選擇。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：你在旅行筆記中畫失敗一頁，原想把整本棄掉；重看卻發現記下光線的文字仍有用。你想寫反思，保留那頁作學習，並用下一頁再試，而非宣稱每幅都會畫好。用一至兩句英文表達。

examples.en: One failed sketch does not write my whole future. I will keep the notes about the light and try another view on the next page.
examples.zh: 一幅失敗速寫未寫定我整個未來；我會保留光線筆記，在下一頁再試另一景物。

examples.en: This disappointing page need not write my whole future. I can learn from it without discarding the useful observations or promising that the next sketch will be perfect.
examples.zh: 這頁令人失望的作品不必寫定我往後畫畫的整個未來；我可從中學習，不丟掉有用觀察，也不保證下一幅完美。

writing.selfCheckZh: 承認這頁失望，保留有用觀察及再試選擇，不把一次失敗推成永遠不會，也不保證下次完美。

takeaways.en: One difficult rehearsal did not write their whole future as a group; they agreed to try a different division of work.
takeaways.zh: 一次艱難排練未寫定小組整個未來；他們議定試另一種分工。

takeaways.en: The rejected proposal did not write my whole future, though I still had to find another way to fund the project.
takeaways.zh: 提案被拒未寫定我整個未來，但我仍需另找項目資助方法。
